title: Pokémon Pokopia Habitat Guide: How to Build Every Habitat
description: Learn everything about building habitats, managing resources, and understanding the Habitat Dex in Pokémon Pokopia. Includes requirements for early-game habitats.
content: title: "Pokopia Habitats Building Guide (2026): Upgrade Paths, Costs, Comfort, and Priority Strategy" description: "Learn Pokopia habitat mechanics: upgrade tiers, resource costs per tier, Comfort building strategies, type-specific habitat bonuses, and which habitats to prioritize in each game phase." keywords: ["pokopia habitats", "pokopia habitat building", "pokopia habitat upgrade", "pokopia habitat type"] date: 2026-04-06 author: Pokopia Guide Team lastUpdated: 2026-04-06 Pokémon Pokopia Habitat Guide Mastering the art of building is essential for any successful trainer. In Pokémon Pokopia , a Habitat is a specific arrangement of plants, items, and furniture. When you place the right combination of items, you create a home that attracts specific Pokémon! With over 200 habitats to discover, building diverse environments is the key to completing your Pokédex. Habitats in Pokémon Pokopia are far more than Pokémon storage. They are production centers, comfort engines, and long-term resource multipliers. Building habitats efficiently means understanding upgrade costs, Comfort mechanics, and which habitats unlock which specialties. This guide breaks down the economics of habitat upgrades and helps you prioritize which habitats to build when. TL;DR Start with one starter habitat and expand to 3-4 by hour 20. Each habitat upgrade tier inflates costs (Tier 1: 10 lumber; Tier 2: 20 ore; Tier 3: 50 ore + rare materials). Comfort threshold unlocks (50+, 100+, 150+) grant production bonuses and visiting Pokémon bonuses—these ROI faster than construction speed alone. Prioritize habitats by specialty unlock, not by prettiness: Build + Collect habitats first, then type-specialized habitats (Fire, Water). Habitat Basics What Do Habitats Do? House Pokémon : Store multiple Pokémon in one habitat (capacity scales with Comfort) Generate Resources : Housed Pokémon passively produce items tied to their type and specialty Build Comfort : Pokémon receive Comfort from habitat environment (type match, decor, flavor foods) Unlock Bonuses : At Comfort milestones (50, 100, 150), Pokémon activate special perks—production boosters, visitor attraction, evolution triggers Habitat Tiers (1-4) Each habitat level increases capacity, production rate, and unlocks advanced decor/specialty combinations. Tier Build Cost Capacity Production Rate Special Unlock Tier 1 10 Lumber 3 Pokémon 1× Basic comfort system Tier 2 20 Iron Ore 6 Pokémon 1.2× Type matching bonus Tier 3 50 Iron Ore + 10 Copper 10 Pokémon 1.5× Specialty building bonus Tier 4 100 Pokemetal + 20 Gold Ore 15 Pokémon 2.0× Master habitat—all bonuses active Comfort Mechanics Comfort is the core ecosystem. Higher Comfort = more production, more visitors, more activity. What Raises Comfort? Type Matching (e.g., Fire-type Pokémon in a Fire habitat): +5 Comfort per Pokémon Flavor Matching (e.g., Dry food to a Dry-preferring Pokémon): +10 Comfort per food gift Decorations (e.g., themed decor in Fire habitats): +1-2 Comfort per decoration Specialty Synergies (housing Build specialty Pokémon in construction-heavy habitats): +5 Comfort and productivity Comfort Thresholds and Bonuses Comfort Bonus Effect Gameplay Impact 50+ Type production boost (+20%) Basic Pokémon start generating type-specific items 100+ Visitor attraction (+50% chance) Random Pokémon from other habitats visit, boosting their Comfort too 150+ Master bonus (unlocks evolution variants) Special habitat evolutions trigger; production output multiplied 200+ Peak state All bonuses stack; max production; rare spawns more common info You don't need 200 Comfort everywhere. Focusing on reaching 100 Comfort in 2-3 specialized habitats is more efficient than spreading effort across 10 habitats. What is a Habitat? A Habitat is triggered when you place specific items in close proximity. Once the requirements are met, the area transforms, and you'll see grass shaking or Pokémon appearing shortly after. Pro-Tip : Rare Pokémon have a lower spawn rate. Building multiple instances of the same habitat improves your chances of finding them! Habitat Priority Strategy Phase 0-1 (Hours 0-5): The Starter Build : 1 Tier 1 Starter Habitat Pokémon : Your initial team Goal : Just survive; focus on story progression, not optimization Phase 1 (Hours 5-15): The Anchor Setup Build : 1 Fire habitat (Tier 1-2) + 1 Water habitat (Tier 1) Rationale : Fire habitats unlock burn-based production; Water habitats unlock farming and decoration elements Comfort Target : 50+ in Fire habitat (unlocks Burn specialty training) Specialties to House : One Build specialist and one Collect specialist Phase 2 (Hours 15-40): The Production Scaling Build : Add 2-3 specialized habitats (e.g., Psychic, Grass, Electric) Upgrade Target : Bring Fire and Water habitats to Tier 2-3 Comfort Target : 100+ in 2 habitats (unlock visitor bonuses) Specialties to House : Prioritize Recycle and Litter specialists Phase 3 (Hours 40+): The Late-Game Specialization Build : Max to 6-8 habitats, each type-specific (Fire, Water, Psychic, Grass, Rock, Electric, Dark, Steel) Upgrade Target : All core habitats to Tier 3-4 Comfort Target : 150+ in 4-5 habitats (unlock master bonuses) Specialties to House : Mix-and-match based on current production bottleneck Cost Analysis: When to Upgrade vs. Build New Building a new Tier 1 habitat costs 10 lumber. Upgrading a Tier 1 to Tier 2 costs 20 ore. By hour 15, ore is abundant-enough that upgrading is faster than building from scratch. Decision Framework: Upgrade Scenario Cost ROI Upgrade Tier 1 → Tier 2 (ore available) 20 ore + 5 hrs craft time +20% production; faster ROI Build new Tier 1 (need more Pokémon storage) 10 lumber + 2 hrs craft time +1 habitat slot; planning-dependent Ignore upgrade, focus on story 0 Slower long-term production Rule of Thumb : By hour 20, always upgrade over building. You'll have 3-4 habitats, and Tier 2 production > Tier 1 × 5. Early Game Habitat List (Habitat Dex) Advanced: Specialty Habitat Synergies Certain Pokémon specialties amplify when grouped in matching-type habitats: Build + Construct Specialties Housing a Build specialist in a construction-heavy habitat (one with multiple upgrades in progress): Builds complete 50% faster Generated resources = 25% bonus building materials Collect + Farming Habitats Housing Collect in a Water/Grass habitat: Doubled item output from habitat production Crop yields increase by 25% Recycle + Trash/Item Habitats Housing Recycle in a Psychic/Dark habitat: Unused items convert to currency (10-50% efficiency) Production chains self-sustain longer between harvests Common Mistakes Mistake 1: Building Too Many Habitats Too Fast Spreading resources across 6+ habitats by hour 20 forces 1-2 Pokémon per habitat (low Comfort). Better: 3-4 habitats, well-stocked and high Comfort. Mistake 2: Ignoring Type Matching Housing Fire Pokémon in a Water habitat = half Comfort gain. Type matching is highest ROI Comfort multiplier. Mistake 3: Delaying Upgrades Leaving habitats at Tier 1 past hour 20 is a pacing mistake. Tier 2 upgrades pay off within 5 hours of unlock. Mistake 4: Decorating Before Comfort Decorations are fun but low-impact vs. housing matching Pokémon types. Save decor for hour 30+. Related Guides and Specialties Pokopia Best Builds Guide Pokopia Dry Flavors Guide Build Specialty FAQ How many habitats should I have by hour 30? 3-4 habitats (including starter), all at least Tier 1, with 1-2 at Tier 2. What's the fastest way to reach 100 Comfort? Type matching + flavor gifts. House type-matching Pokémon and gift their preferred flavors every 2-3 hours. Is it worth upgrading Tier 2 → Tier 3 before building new habitats? Only if you're focusing on production scaling. If you need more Pokémon storage, build new Tier 1 first. Which specialty habitat should I build first? Fire or Water. Both unlock production chains early. Build in this order: Fire → Water → Psychic. Early Game Habitat List (Habitat Dex) Here are the most common habitats you'll need to build when starting your journey in the Withered Wasteland : ID Habitat Name Requirements Attracted Pokémon 001 Tall Grass Habitat 4x Tall Grass tiles Bulbasaur, Charmander, Squirtle 002 Tree-Shaded Tall Grass 1x Large Tree + 4x Tall Grass Scyther, Heracross 003 Boulder-Shaded Grass 1x Boulder + 4x Tall Grass Timburr 005 Seaside Tall Grass 4x Tall Grass + 2x Ocean Water Water-type Pokémon 007 Illuminated Tall Grass 4x Tall Grass + 1x Lighting Item Rare Night Pokémon 008 Pretty Flower Bed 4x Wildflowers Flower-loving Pokémon 010 Hydrated Flower Bed 4x Flowers + Beside Water Water/Grass types How to Build Your First Habitat 1. Gather Materials Most early habitats require Tall Grass or Flowers . You can create these using moves: Leafage : Use this move (Press ZR to switch) to create grass or flower tiles on the ground. Water Gun : Use this to water saplings to turn them into Large Trees . 2. Placement Strategy Habitat items must be "bunched together" in a small plot. For example, to make a Tree-Shaded Tall Grass Habitat (required for the Lumber quest), stand near a tree and place 4 grass tiles directly around its base. 3. Real-Time Construction One of the most important things to remember is that construction is tied to real-world time . Patience is Key : Once you've placed the items, your Pokémon will begin building. For larger structures, this can take several hours. Planning : For more details on how time affects your progress, see our Game Length & Time Mechanics Guide . 3. Monitoring for Spawns After building, keep an eye on the habitat. Shaking Grass : Indicates a Pokémon is about to appear. Speech Bubbles : Some Pokémon (like Scyther) will appear with a request bubble. Talk to them to unlock new moves or items! Bulldozing Mechanics If you make a mistake or want to redesign your ranch, you can use the Bulldoze function. Resource Refund : Unlike many games, Pokopia is generous! Bulldozing items often returns a portion of the materials used, allowing you to iterate on your designs without losing everything. Clearing Space : Use Bulldoze to clear old habitats to make room for high-level specialized environments as you progress. Advanced Tips for Habitat Builders Environmental Level : Many habitats only unlock or successfully attract Pokémon once your ranch reaches a certain Environment Level. Real-Time Clock : Some Pokémon only appear in habitats at specific times of day (Day/Night cycles). Redundancy : If a "Very Rare" Pokémon isn't appearing, don't delete the habitat! Build a second or third one nearby to stack the spawn probabilities.

title: More Spores for Hoppip Event Guide: Habitats & Mechanics
description: Everything you need to know about the More Spores for Hoppip event in Pokémon Pokopia, including how to visit Dream Islands and habitat recipes.
content: The More Spores for Hoppip event is the first limited-time event in Pokémon Pokopia . During this springtime celebration, trainers can befriend the Hoppip evolutionary line, which is otherwise unavailable in the wild. This guide covers the event schedule, the unique Cotton Spore collection mechanic, and the specific habitat recipes required to summon Hoppip, Skiploom, and Jumpluff. Event Schedule & Participation The introductory event: More Spores for Hoppip. Start Date : Tuesday, March 10 at 5:00 AM local time End Date : Wednesday, March 25 at 4:59 AM local time How to Participate To start the event, you must have a fully repaired Pokemon Center in one of your main town areas. Look for a Hoppip standing inside the Pokemon Center and speak to it to initiate the event activities. [!NOTE] Event features are currently unavailable on Cloud Islands (multiplayer islands). You must be in the main campaign areas to participate. Collecting Cotton Spores The core loop of the event involves collecting Cotton Spores , which act as the event currency. How to Visit Dream Islands Cotton Spores only appear on Dream Islands . To access these islands: Obtain any Doll item. Find Drifloon in your world and give it the doll. Drifloon will transport you to a Dream Island where Cotton Spores spawn abundantly. Once collected, you can exchange these spores at the Pokemon Center shop for exclusive Picnic-themed items needed for habitat building. Event Item Exchanges You can exchange your Cotton Spores for the following items: Item Name Quantity Received Necessary Items Dandy flower seeds 5 5 Cotton spores Flowery table setting 1 10 Cotton spores Flower table 1 10 Cotton spores Flower cushion 1 10 Cotton spores Picnic Blanket 1 15 Cotton spores Hoppip Water Bottle 1 5 Cotton spores Lunch box 1 5 Cotton spores Juice trio 1 5 Cotton spores Flower backpack 1 5 Cotton spores Flower garland 10 5 Cotton spores Event Habitat Recipes To attract the featured Pokemon, you can arrange items in a 2x2 grid layout . Habitat Construction: Place your event items in a 2x2 grid as shown above to attract Hoppip, Skiploom, or Jumpluff. 1. Yellow Carpet (Attracts Hoppip & Line) A simple but effective habitat for all members of the Hoppip family. Components : 4x Dandy Flowers Layout : Place the 4 flowers in a 2x2 square. 2. Field-Trip Friends (Attracts Skiploom) Specifically designed to increase the spawn rate of Skiploom. Components : 1x Flower Backpack + 1x Lunch Box + 1x Hoppip Water Bottle Layout : Arrange these three items within a 2x2 grid (one slot will remain empty or can be filled with a flower). 3. Dandelion Lunchtime (Attracts Jumpluff) The premium habitat for encountering the final evolution, Jumpluff. Components : 1x Dandy Flowers + 1x Flower Cushion + 1x Flowery Table Setting + 1x Lunch Box Layout : Fill all four slots of a 2x2 grid with these four items. Featured Pokemon Pokemon Habitat Requirement Rarity Hoppip Yellow Carpet Common Skiploom Yellow Carpet / Field-Trip Friends Uncommon Jumpluff Yellow Carpet / Dandelion Lunchtime Rare [!TIP] Since this is a limited-time event, focus on collecting enough Cotton Spores early to unlock the Dandelion Lunchtime items, as Jumpluff is significantly harder to find without the dedicated habitat.

title: Pokemon Pokopia Guide: How To Befriend Mew & Mewtwo
description: Step-by-step guide to unlocking Mew and Mewtwo in Pokemon Pokopia, from Sparkling Skylands to Dream Islands.
content: Getting Mew and Mewtwo into your village in Pokemon Pokopia is one of the most satisfying goals in the game. These two Legendaries sit at entries 299 and 300 in your Pokedex, and earning their friendship requires patience, the right resources, and knowing exactly where to look. Neither encounter is gated behind difficult combat, but both demand real effort across multiple game systems. Here is everything you need to know to bring these iconic Pokemon home. How Do You Unlock Mewtwo in Pokemon Pokopia? Before you can even think about befriending Mewtwo , you need to reach the Sparkling Skylands , the final area of Pokemon Pokopia . If you have not unlocked it yet, focus on progressing through the main story first. There is no shortcut here. Once you arrive in the Sparkling Skylands, your first task is building the Waterside Dinghy habitat to meet Dragonite . This will be one of the first objectives the game hands you upon arrival. After completing it, head to the island featuring the tall metal tower to begin Tinkatuff 's storyline. Work through Tinkatuff 's quests until the game asks you to restore the Skyland Building . Completing that restoration leads you to the top floor, where you will encounter Mewtwo for the first time and add it to your Pokedex. danger Meeting Mewtwo at the top of the Skyland Building adds it to your Pokedex, but it will NOT move into any of your villages automatically. You still need to complete the Dream Island step. Mewtwo 's Pokedex entry screen How To Restore the Skyland Building Restoring the Skyland Building works the same as other construction projects in Pokopia , except it is split across multiple floors. Each floor requires a separate set of materials and takes one full in-game day to complete. Plan ahead and gather resources in advance to avoid unnecessary delays. Floor Materials Required 2F 25 Concrete , 10 Glass , 5 Pokemetal , 10 Iron Ingot 3F 25 Concrete , 10 Glass , 10 Glowing Stone , 15 Copper Ingot 4F 40 Concrete , 15 Glass , 10 Paper , 10 Brick , 20 Lumber info If you want to skip the one-day construction wait between floors, you can use your Nintendo Switch 2's system settings to time travel forward. This is a legitimate method many players use to speed up building projects in Pokopia . Once all floors are restored, you will be sent on a quest to the top of the building, triggering the first Mewtwo encounter. How To Get Mewtwo To Move Into Your Village After the Skyland Building encounter, Mewtwo will not settle in your village on its own. To make that happen, you need to find it on a Dragonite Dream Island . You can access Dream Islands using either a Dragonite or a Ditto Poke Doll . Mewtwo 's exact location on these islands is randomized, but it almost always appears behind enclosed walls built from various materials . Break through those walls, speak with Mewtwo, and invite it back to your village. Here is what makes Mewtwo particularly flexible compared to other Legendaries: No dedicated habitat required. Mewtwo does not need a special biome or structure. It settles comfortably in a standard Tall Grass habitat or any available home slot. After accepting your invitation, Mewtwo will initially follow you back to wherever Drifloon dropped you off, and it will continue following you if you move to new areas. info Because Mewtwo has no habitat requirement, it is one of the easier Legendaries to place once you actually befriend it. The hard part is getting to that Dream Island encounter. How Do You Befriend Mew in Pokemon Pokopia? Based on available source information, the specifics of befriending Mew follow a similar structure to Mewtwo , relying on the Dream Island system as the core mechanic for bringing Legendary Pokemon into your village. Mew is entry 300 in the Pokedex, making it the final Pokemon in Pokopia's roster. The Dream Island system, accessed via Dragonite or Ditto Poke Doll , is the primary way to encounter and invite Legendary Pokemon to your village. Mew's location on Dream Islands is random, consistent with how other Legendaries behave in this system. warning Dream Island encounters for Legendary Pokemon like Mew and Mewtwo are not guaranteed on every visit. If Mew does not appear during one trip, you will need to try again on a subsequent Dream Island run.

title: Pokemon Pokopia Guide: How to Befriend the Kanto Legendary Birds
description: Attract Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres to your islands in Pokemon Pokopia with this step-by-step habitat building guide.
content: The Kanto Legendary Birds, Articuno , Zapdos , and Moltres , are among the most iconic Pokemon ever created, and Pokemon Pokopia gives you a real chance to have all three living on your islands. The catch? Getting them there is a much bigger undertaking than dropping a few grass patches. These are full construction projects that demand serious materials, a skilled crew, and a trip to a late-game area. Here's exactly what you need to do. All three Kanto birds together Where Do You Find the Kanto Legendary Bird Blueprints? Before any construction begins, you need the blueprints. All three building recipes are located in Palette Town , which sits over the bridge from the Withered Wasteland . You can technically visit Palette Town at any point, but be realistic: the materials required are deep late-game resources, so there is no rush to head there early. Once you arrive, you will notice that Palette Town is split into three distinct land masses . Each one has a steep hill near its center, and at the top of each hill sits one of the three blueprints. Climb each hill and collect them all. That's the easy part. info You can grab all three blueprints in a single visit to Palette Town. There is no reason to make multiple trips, so clear your inventory space and collect everything at once. What Materials Do You Need for Each Legendary Bird Habitat? Each of the three buildings has its own material list and its own crew requirements. None of them are quick builds, and the Pokemetal requirement alone will take significant grinding. Here is the full breakdown: Building Materials Required Pokemon Crew Required Freezing Chambers ( Articuno ) Stone x50, Ice x50, Crystal Fragment x10, Pokemetal x10 Build Specialty x1, Water Specialty x1, Search Specialty x1, Crush Specialty x1, Others x11 Abandoned Power Plant ( Zapdos ) Copper Ingot x50, Iron Ingot x50, Sea Glass Fragments x50, Brick x50, Pokemetal x10 Build Specialty x1, Fly Specialty x1, Generate Specialty x1, Crush Specialty x1, Others x11 Altar of Flame ( Moltres ) Copper Ingot x50, Gold Ingot x50, Lava Rock x50, Pokemetal x10 Build Specialty x1, Fly Specialty x1, Burn Specialty x1, Crush Specialty x1, Others x11 Each building requires 15 total Pokemon on the construction crew, with four specialty roles filled and eleven general workers rounding out the team. Make sure you have the right specialty Pokemon assigned before starting each project. warning These habitats take up a massive footprint on your islands. Before placing them, use Rollout to flatten the terrain and clear enough space. Trying to squeeze them into an unprepared area will cause problems. Zapdos Power Plant build screen How To Build Habitats for Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres Once you have the blueprints and materials ready, the actual placement is flexible. The most practical approach is to stay in Palette Town and build on the land masses there, since each island already has a patch of terrain that can be cleared and expanded with minimal effort. That said, you are not locked into Palette Town. Any location on your islands with enough flat space will work. Building the Freezing Chambers for Articuno The Freezing Chambers are Articuno 's home, and they demand a mix of Stone , Ice , Crystal Fragments , and Pokemetal . The crew needs a Water Specialty Pokemon and a Search Specialty Pokemon alongside the standard Build and Crush roles. Stock up on Crystal Fragments before starting, as they can be the trickiest resource to gather in bulk. Building the Abandoned Power Plant for Zapdos The Abandoned Power Plant has the longest material list of the three, requiring Copper Ingots , Iron Ingots , Sea Glass Fragments , Bricks , and Pokemetal . The Generate Specialty crew role is unique to this build , so identify which Pokemon in your roster carries that specialty before you start gathering materials. Building the Altar of Flame for Moltres The Altar of Flame calls for Copper Ingots , Gold Ingots , Lava Rock , and Pokemetal . The Burn Specialty role is the key crew requirement here. Gold Ingots and Lava Rock both point to volcanic or high-temperature resource areas, so plan your gathering runs accordingly. danger All three buildings require Pokemetal x10 each, meaning you need 30 Pokemetal total if you plan to build all three. Prioritize farming this resource early so it does not become a bottleneck late in the process. What Do You Get for Befriending All Three Kanto Legendary Birds? Beyond the satisfaction of having Articuno , Zapdos , and Moltres on your islands, there is a concrete reward waiting once you befriend all three. Completing the trio unlocks the recipe for a Tidal Bell , which is a key item needed to befriend Lugia . So if adding the legendary sea guardian to your collection is on your list, the Kanto birds are not optional. They are the prerequisite. info The Tidal Bell recipe is only handed over after all three birds are befriended, not after each individual one. Finish the full set before expecting that reward to appear. Tips for Preparing Your Island Before You Build A few practical steps will make the whole process much smoother: Flatten terrain early. Use Rollout on your chosen build sites before you even start gathering materials. The last thing you want is to have everything ready and then discover the land is too uneven. Assign crew before gathering. Check which specialty Pokemon you already own before deciding which habitat to build first. Start with whichever one your current roster best supports. Farm Pokemetal in batches. Since all three habitats share this requirement, gathering all 30 Pokemetal in one focused session is far more efficient than doing three separate runs. Stay organized in Palette Town. Building all three habitats in Palette Town keeps things tidy and makes the most of the pre-existing terrain on each land mass there.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Befriend with Ho-Oh & Lugia
description: Unlock Ho-Oh and Lugia in Pokémon Pokopia by crafting the Clear Bell and Tidal Bell. Here's every step you need.
content: Ho-Oh and Lugia are two of the most iconic Legendary Pokémon in the entire franchise, and spotting them soaring overhead in Pokémon Pokopia is genuinely thrilling. What most players don't realize is that those flyovers aren't just eye candy. You can actually call both of them down, speak to them, and register them to your Pokédex. It takes serious preparation, but this guide walks you through every requirement, material, and step to make it happen. What Do You Need Before You Can Befriend Ho-Oh or Lugia? Before crafting either bell, two conditions apply to both Legendaries: Complete the main story. You must finish all Important Requests and roll credits. Neither bell recipe unlocks until the endgame is cleared. Collect feathers and Rare Pokémetal. Both bells require 5x Rare Pokémetal each, plus the specific feathers tied to each Legendary. Beyond those shared requirements, each Legendary has its own additional condition tied to recruiting other Legendary Pokémon first. Ho-Oh registered in Pokédex info Ho-Oh drops Rainbow Feathers and Lugia drops Silver Feathers during their random flyovers throughout the game. Pick these up whenever you see them so you're not scrambling for materials at endgame. How to Befriend Ho-Oh Step 1: Meet the Three Legendary Beasts To unlock the Clear Bell recipe, you must first meet Raikou , Entei , and Suicune , the three Legendary Beasts found on the Dream Islands. These roaming Legendaries are well-hidden, much like their original appearances in the Game Boy Color era, so tracking them down takes patience. Once you've encountered all three Legendary Beasts, the Clear Bell recipe automatically unlocks. Step 2: Craft the Clear Bell With the recipe in hand, head to your crafting menu and gather : 5x Rainbow Feathers 5x Rare Pokémetal Step 3: Call Down Ho-Oh Wait for Ho-Oh to appear flying overhead. When it does, place the Clear Bell on the ground and ring it. Ho-Oh will descend, greet you, and be added to your Pokédex. How to Befriend Lugia: Tidal Bell Guide Step 1: Meet the Three Legendary Birds To unlock the Tidal Bell recipe, you need to meet Articuno , Zapdos , and Moltres , the Kanto Legendary Bird trio. Fans of Pokémon the Movie 2000 will recognize this connection immediately, as Lugia's bond with the three birds is classic Pokémon lore brought to life in Pokopia. Meeting each bird requires building their altars. The altar building kits are found at Palette Town . Once you place an altar, wait for the corresponding Legendary Bird to appear at that location. Repeat this for all three birds to unlock the Tidal Bell recipe. Step 2: Craft the Tidal Bell With all three birds met, gather the following: 5x Silver Feathers 5x Rare Pokémetal Step 3: Call Down Lugia Wait for Lugia to fly overhead, place the Tidal Bell on the ground, and ring it. Lugia will make its entrance and join your Pokédex. danger Both bells can only be crafted after completing the main story. Don't worry if the recipes don't appear in your crafting menu mid-game — this is intentional. How Do You Get Rainbow Feathers and Silver Feathers? Both feather types drop randomly when Ho-Oh and Lugia fly overhead during normal gameplay. Ho-Oh scatters Rainbow Feathers and Lugia scatters Silver Feathers . After a flyover, look for the feathers on the ground and collect them. Some players report needing to use the Cut ability to access certain feather drop locations, so keep that in mind if a feather appears out of reach. You need exactly 5 of each feather type, so collecting them passively while progressing through the story is the most efficient approach. info Prioritize getting Rare Pokémetal early. You need 10 total (5 for each bell), and it can take time to farm. Check the Pokémetal guide for the fastest farming locations.

title: Pokemon Pokopia Guide: How to Befriend with Raikou, Entei, & Suicune
description: Track down Raikou, Entei, and Suicune in Pokemon Pokopia with this step-by-step Dream Island guide to unlock Ho-Oh's Clear Bell recipe.
content: Raikou , Entei , and Suicune are among the most beloved Legendaries in Pokemon history, and Pokemon Pokopia does them justice by hiding all three across secret cave dens tucked inside Dream Islands. Unlike most Pokemon in the game, these three don't show up in a fixed habitat or through a straightforward story beat. Finding them takes preparation, the right Poke Dolls, and a bit of patience since their appearances aren't guaranteed every visit. What Do You Need Before Searching for the Legendary Dogs? Before heading out to any Dream Island, there are two requirements you need to tick off first. First , you must have access to Dream Islands through Drifloon . You unlock this during the Withered Wasteland story arc. Head to the coast near the bridge leading to Palette Town, where Drifloon is floating. Build a habitat using three lit campfires and locate the Poke Doll on the opposite side of the Withered Wastelands to bring Drifloon into your village. Second , you need to progress far enough in the main story to encounter Raikou at Bleak Beach . This story meeting adds Raikou to your Pokedex automatically, but it does not bring Raikou into your village. It does, however, appear to be the trigger that makes all three Legendary Dogs available on Dream Islands at all. danger Meeting Raikou at Bleak Beach only registers a Pokedex entry. To actually befriend Raikou and add them to your village, you still need to find them on the correct Dream Island. Third , you'll need Cooking unlocked and the ability to make Hamburger Steaks , which boost Rock Smash . This skill is essential for breaking through the blocked cave walls where each dog hides. Unlock Dream Islands via Drifloon Which Poke Dolls Do You Need? Each Legendary Dog is tied to a specific Dream Island, and each island requires its own Poke Doll to access. You can find the Pikachu Doll and Eevee Doll in Bleak Beach, and all three can be purchased from the Palette Town Pokemon Center as your Environment Level rises. Glowing spots on the ground may also yield Dolls at random. Legendary Dog Dream Island Required Poke Doll Raikou Ocean Dream Island Pikachu Doll Entei Volcanic Dream Island Arcanine Doll Suicune Wasteland Dream Island Eevee Doll info Purchase all three Dolls from the Palette Town Pokemon Center early so you're never blocked from visiting any island when the opportunity arises. How to Find Raikou on the Ocean Dream Island With the Pikachu Doll in hand, travel to the Ocean Dream Island . Make your way toward the central mountain and drop into the cave system at its heart. Follow the paths downward, and keep an eye out for an area lined with steel blocks featuring gaps in the wall. That blocked-off section is Raikou 's den. Use Rock Smash to break through, speak to Raikou , then return to Drifloon to leave the island. Before you go, grab the 3x Rare Pokemetal sitting on the pedestal behind Raikou. That material is genuinely useful, so don't skip it. warning Raikou does not appear on every visit to the Ocean Dream Island. If the steel-block den is absent, return the next day or adjust your system clock forward by one day to trigger a new island seed. How to Find Entei on the Volcanic Dream Island The Arcanine Doll takes you to the Volcanic Dream Island , a lava-cracked mountain that looks far more dangerous on the outside than it actually is inside. Head straight for the mountain entrance and descend through the cave passages. When you spot a corner sealed off by Lava Blocks , you've found Entei . Smash through, take a moment to appreciate having a Fire-type Legendary in front of you, then speak to Entei to bring them back with you. Collect the 3x Rare Pokemetal from the pedestal before departing. How to Find Suicune on the Wasteland Dream Island Suicune hides on the Wasteland Dream Island , accessed via the Eevee Doll . Despite the unglamorous setting, the process is the same. Head to the rocky central area, enter the cave system, and walk until you spot Ice blocks blocking a passage. Ice is a rare material in Pokopia , so grab any loose pieces you see along the way. Break through the ice barrier to reach Suicune , speak to them, and head back to Drifloon. The 3x Rare Pokemetal on the pedestal here is just as valuable as the other two, so make sure to collect it. How Do You Know If a Legendary Dog Is Present? Spawns are not guaranteed on any visit. Here's the most reliable way to check without wandering the entire cave system: Open your Pokedex after arriving on the island. Set the search filter to All with Location: This Area . If a ? symbol appears in the results, a Legendary is present on that island. If no ? shows up, the dog isn't there this visit. Return the next calendar day or use the system clock workaround to advance time. info The three dogs have no natural habitat type, which means once you bring them back to your village, they can be housed comfortably in Tall Grass without needing a specialized biome. Check for Legendaries via Pokedex What Is the Reward for Befriending All Legendary Dogs? Once all three dogs are living in your village, the game rewards you with the recipe for a Clear Bell . Players familiar with Pokemon Gold , Silver , Crystal , or the Gen 4 remakes already know exactly what this item leads to. The Clear Bell is the key ingredient required to befriend Ho-Oh , one of the rarest Legendary encounters in all of Pokemon Pokopia . Beyond the Ho-Oh unlock, having Raikou , Entei , and Suicune as village residents is its own reward. These three are some of the most iconic Legendaries in the franchise, and watching them roam your Tall Grass habitat never gets old.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Break & Move Large Boulder Rocks
description: Learn how to make, move, and destroy Large Boulder Rocks in Pokémon Pokopia, including how to use the 3D Printer, Strength ability, Magnet Rise, and upgraded Rock Smash.
content: Large Boulder Rocks are one of the bigger environmental objects players will encounter in Pokémon Pokopia . Unlike most decorations and terrain objects, these rocks come with several limitations that can make them confusing to use at first. Players can place them around their island, build habitats near them, or remove them to clear space. However, the process for making, moving, or destroying Large Boulder Rocks is not immediately obvious. This guide explains exactly how Large Boulder Rocks work in Pokémon Pokopia and the different ways players can interact with them. How to Make Large Boulder Rocks Large Boulder Rocks cannot be crafted normally in Pokémon Pokopia. Instead, players need to duplicate them using the 3D Printer inside a Pokémon Center . Before this becomes available, players must first rebuild at least one Pokémon Center somewhere on the map . Once the Pokémon Center is active, the 3D Printer can be used to create objects that have been photographed. To create a Large Boulder Rock, players must first capture a reference photo of one. Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Break & Move Large Boulder Rocks Open the camera using the “-” button on the Nintendo Switch controller , then press “Y” to enter reference photo mode . While in this mode, take a picture of a Large Boulder Rock . The object will be labeled through the camera interface. After taking the photo, return to the Pokémon Center and interact with the 3D Printer . The rock will appear in the list of captured objects. Players can then exchange the required amount of Pokémetal to print a Large Boulder Rock. Once printed, the rock is added to the player’s inventory and can be placed like other decorative objects. However, once placed, Large Boulder Rocks cannot be picked up again normally , so it’s best to decide the placement carefully. How to Move Large Boulder Rocks Moving Large Boulder Rocks in Pokémon Pokopia is possible, but the options are limited. There are currently two main methods players can use. The first method involves learning the Strength ability from Machoke in Rocky Ridges . Once Strength is unlocked, players can push Large Boulder Rocks by holding the “A” button and moving in a direction . Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Break & Move Large Boulder Rocks This allows players to reposition the rock slightly, but the movement is restricted. Rocks can only be pushed along the ground and cannot be freely rotated or placed exactly where players might want them. The second method becomes available much later in the game through Magnemite ’s Transform ability using Magnet Rise . This ability provides far more precise object control, allowing players to hover and reposition objects more accurately . However, Magnet Rise is unlocked only during the post-game after completing the Team Initiation Challenge , making it a late-game solution for advanced building and terraforming. How to Destroy Large Boulder Rocks If players want to completely remove a Large Boulder Rock, they cannot rely on the standard Rock Smash ability. Instead, they must first upgrade Rock Smash using buffs obtained through cooking. After reaching Rocky Ridges and rescuing Chef Dente , players unlock the cooking system. Among the early recipes are burgers , which temporarily enhance Ditto ’s Rock Smash ability. With the upgraded Rock Smash active, players can break tougher environmental objects, including: Iron Ore blocks Gold Ore blocks Large Boulder Rocks Lava Rocks Once destroyed, the Large Boulder Rock does not drop another Boulder item . Instead, players receive a small amount of Stones as materials. This means destroying the rock is mainly useful for clearing terrain or gathering resources , rather than relocating the object. Final Tips for Using Large Boulder Rocks Large Boulder Rocks are mostly used for environment design and habitat building in Pokémon Pokopia. Because they cannot be picked up after placement, players should plan their builds carefully before placing one. Early in the game, players will mainly rely on Strength to push rocks around , while late-game players can use Magnet Rise for more accurate positioning . If space is needed, an upgraded Rock Smash can remove the rock entirely. Understanding these mechanics makes it much easier to manage terrain and design better habitats across the Pokopia map.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Bubbly Basin Guide: How to Find the Windup Inkay
description: Find the Windup Inkay in Pokémon Pokopia's Bubbly Basin fast. Learn its exact location, how to reach it, and which Pokémon it helps you spawn.
content: Pokémon Pokopia added a lot of new items and collectibles with the first wave of the Expansion Pass, and the Windup Inkay is one of the trickier ones to track down. It sits hidden deep inside the Bubbly Basin area, tucked behind a couple of environmental obstacles that are easy to walk right past if you do not know what to look for. Here is exactly where to go and what to do once you get there. The Windup Inkay is located inside a large crevice in the middle of Bubbly Basin . Drop down into the ravine and work your way along the right-hand side. You are looking for a pile of sand that partially blocks what appears to be a dead end. That sand pile is actually hiding a secondary tunnel corridor, so push through it. The crevice entrance in Bubbly Basin Once inside the tunnel, you will spot breakable rocks on the right wall . This is where Ditto 's Rock Smash ability comes in. Smash through those rocks to open up a hidden chamber behind them. Inside that chamber, there is a Poké Ball sitting on the floor , and picking it up gives you a constructed Windup Inkay ready to use. Step-by-step path to the Windup Inkay Head into the large crevice at the center of Bubbly Basin Follow the right-hand side of the ravine until you see a sand pile blocking a tunnel entrance Enter the hidden tunnel corridor behind the sand Use Ditto 's Rock Smash on the breakable rocks along the right wall Collect the Windup Inkay from the Poké Ball inside the revealed chamber important You need Ditto 's Rock Smash ability to access the hidden chamber. Make sure Ditto is in your party before making the trip. What does the Windup Inkay do in Pokémon Pokopia? The Windup Inkay serves two purposes. First, it functions as a decorative toy that you can place in your environment to raise the comfort level of Pokémon living there. Second, and more importantly for progression, it is a required habitat item for spawning specific Pokémon. Muddy Playtime habitat setup Which Pokémon use the Windup Inkay habitat? The Muddy Playtime habitat requires the Windup Inkay as one of its components. The full list of items needed to build this habitat is: Loading table... Get all four of those in place and you can attract Marshtomp to the habitat. The Muddy Playtime habitat also draws in Inkay itself, which makes sense given the toy. Barboach can also appear in this habitat, though Barboach first needs to be unlocked through story progression before it will show up. tip The Windup Inkay crafting recipe can be purchased at the Pokémon Center if you want to make additional copies rather than relying on the single one found in the crevice. For a full breakdown of every habitat available in the expansion, including spawn requirements and which Pokémon appear where, the Bubbly Basin habitats and Pokémon spawns guide covers everything in detail. Smash rocks to reveal the chamber Is there anything else hidden in Bubbly Basin worth finding? The Windup Inkay is not the only secret tucked away in Bubbly Basin. After testing the area thoroughly, the crevice is worth exploring slowly rather than rushing through. The sand pile hiding the tunnel is easy to overlook on a first pass, and the breakable rocks inside are not obvious unless you are actively looking for them. If you are working through all the collectibles the expansion has to offer, the Starmie Doll location guide is worth checking out next, since that item unlocks Phione and rewards Grubby Pearls and Gold from Dream Islands. For everything else the Bubbly Basin DLC has to offer, the full Pokémon Pokopia strategy guides collection has you covered.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Fix the Withered Wasteland Water Wheels
description: Stuck on the Water Wheel puzzle in Pokémon Pokopia? Learn exactly how to activate both wheels and unlock the water ability.
content: The Withered Wasteland Water Wheel puzzle in Pokémon Pokopia catches a surprising number of players off guard. You can stumble across both wheels early in the game, get one spinning, and then hit a wall with the second. The reason is simple: the game locks the full solution behind a special ability you haven't earned yet. Once you know what to do and when to do it, the whole puzzle clicks into place. Why Can't You Activate Both Wheels Right Away? The puzzle is split into two distinct parts, and the game does not tell you that upfront. The first Water Wheel can be activated relatively early by opening a small channel that redirects water flow into the mechanism. That partial fix gets the first wheel turning, and it can feel like progress, but the second Water Wheel is a different story entirely. The second wheel requires you to physically carry water and deposit it in the correct position. Without the ability to absorb and place water , there is no way to feed the second mechanism. Visiting the area too early just leaves you staring at a stationary wheel with no obvious solution. danger Do not waste time trying to find an environmental workaround for the second wheel. The game intentionally gates this puzzle behind a progression unlock. Come back later. How to Activate the First Wheel Head to the Withered Wasteland area and locate the water wheel setup. Near the first wheel, you will find a small opening or gap in the water channel. Interact with it to open the flow. Water will redirect into the wheel and start it spinning. That is all there is to the first wheel. It is a straightforward environmental interaction, and you can complete this step without any special abilities unlocked. Unlock Piplup 's water ability How to Unlock the Ability for the Second Wheel This is the step that most players miss. To activate the second Water Wheel, you need an ability that lets you suck up water and place it wherever you choose. Here is how to get it: Travel to Bleak Beach and start progressing through the quest line there. Continue far enough through the Bleak Beach quests to unlock Piplup . After unlocking Piplup , complete the Pip Event . Once the Pip Event advances far enough, you gain the water absorption ability. That ability is exactly what the second wheel needs. According to multiple guides covering Pokémon Pokopia , the Pip Event is the specific trigger that grants water manipulation, so do not skip any steps in that quest chain. How to Fix the Second Wheel Once you have the water ability from the Pip Event, return to Withered Wasteland and follow these steps: Locate a body of water in the Withered Wasteland area. Use the absorb action to collect water into your reservoir. Move to the second Water Wheel mechanism. Place the water down in the position that feeds directly into the wheel. Confirm both wheels are now spinning. warning Make sure you are placing the water in the correct feed position for the second wheel. Dropping it in the wrong spot will not trigger the mechanism, and you will need to collect more water and try again. For more puzzle solutions, habitat guides, and tips across Pokémon Pokopia , browse more guides on Pokopia Wiki to keep your playthrough moving forward.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Concrete
description: Learn exactly how to make Concrete in Pokémon Pokopia using Conkeldurr, a Concrete Mixer, and Limestone in Sparkling Skylands.
content: Concrete is one of the most important late-game building materials in Pokémon Pokopia , and if you've just arrived in Sparkling Skylands , you're going to need it sooner than you think. Unlike simpler resources, producing Concrete requires a specific Pokémon, a craftable machine, and a raw material you'll need to harvest yourself. Once you understand the process, though, it's actually straightforward to set up a steady supply. What Do You Need to Make Concrete in Pokémon Pokopia? Before getting into the step-by-step process, here's a quick summary of everything required to produce Concrete in Pokémon Pokopia : Requirement Details Pokémon Conkeldurr (or any Pokémon with the Crush Specialty ) Machine Concrete Mixer (crafted with x2 Iron Ingots ) Raw Material Limestone (found in Sparkling Skylands or Rocky Ridges) Placement Concrete Mixer must be placed near water Output 4 blocks of Concrete per piece of Limestone processed info One piece of Limestone yields four blocks of Concrete , so you don't need to stockpile massive amounts of raw material to build up a solid supply. Conkeldurr habitat setup screen How to Find Conkeldurr in Sparkling Skylands Conkeldurr is the key Pokémon for this entire process, since he has the Crush Specialty needed to operate the Concrete Mixer. To get him on your side, you need to build a Construction-Site Generator habitat in Sparkling Skylands . What Does the Construction-Site Generator Require? The Construction-Site Generator habitat needs the following items placed together: x1 Furnace x1 Iron Pipes x2 Iron Scaffold Here's the good news: there's already a furnace located near the Pokémon Center in Sparkling Skylands. Use that spot to build out the rest of the habitat so you don't need to craft a new furnace from scratch. You can find Iron Pipes and Iron Scaffold either in Sparkling Skylands itself or near the entrance to Rocky Ridges . Once the habitat is active, Conkeldurr will spawn. Walk up and speak to him, and he'll hand over the recipe for the Concrete Mixer . info Even after you've learned the Concrete Mixer recipe, keep Conkeldurr nearby. He's also your most accessible Crush Specialty Pokémon, so you'll want him following you to the machine when it's time to process Limestone. How to Craft and Place the Concrete Mixer With the recipe in hand, crafting the Concrete Mixer is simple. It only costs x2 Iron Ingots , which you should have plenty of by the time you reach Sparkling Skylands. Where Should You Place the Concrete Mixer? Placement matters here. The Concrete Mixer must have its back tube positioned inside water to function. Fortunately, there's a small waterfall pond close to the Construction-Site Generator area in Sparkling Skylands that works perfectly. The game will indicate whether the placement is valid, so watch for that confirmation before finalizing the position. Concrete Mixer placed near water Where to Find Limestone in Pokémon Pokopia Limestone is the raw material that gets processed into Concrete , and you won't run short of it in Pokémon Pokopia . Here's where to find it: Sparkling Skylands : Limestone blocks are spread across the islands in this region, with a particularly dense cluster on the eastern island . Rocky Ridges : Look inside the cave that contains the hot spring for Limestone deposits here. What's the Fastest Way to Harvest Limestone? The quickest harvesting method is using Graveler 's Rollout ability, which can demolish Limestone blocks rapidly. Alternatively, the Rock Smash ability also works for breaking down Limestone. Given how many blocks are available in Sparkling Skylands, you really won't need to travel far to fill your inventory. warning Don't place your Concrete Mixer and then immediately run off to gather Limestone. Have a stockpile ready before you set everything up, so Conkeldurr can start processing right away without unnecessary trips back and forth. How to Actually Make Concrete Once you have everything in place, follow these steps to start producing Concrete : Craft the Concrete Mixer using x2 Iron Ingots at your workbench. Place the Concrete Mixer near water , ensuring the back tube is submerged. Harvest Limestone from Sparkling Skylands or Rocky Ridges. Load the Limestone into the Concrete Mixer. Have Conkeldurr (or another Crush Specialty Pokémon) follow you to the Concrete Mixer. Wait for the Pokémon to begin processing the Limestone. Return after a short while to collect your finished Concrete blocks . Each piece of Limestone processed gives you 4 blocks of Concrete , so even a modest haul of Limestone translates into a solid batch of building material. info While the Concrete Mixer is running, set up a Security Camera nearby and go tackle other tasks on your Pokopia to-do list. There's no need to stand and watch the process.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Glass
description: Learn exactly how to make Glass in Pokémon Pokopia using Sand, Volcanic Ash, or Sandstone in a Smelting Furnace.
content: Glass is one of those crafting materials in Pokémon Pokopia that the game expects you to figure out on your own. No tutorial points you toward it, and yet you need it for specific crafting recipes and Pokémon Center rebuilds. Once you know where to look and what to toss into the furnace, producing Glass becomes a reliable part of your resource loop. How Do You Make Glass in Pokémon Pokopia? To make Glass in Pokémon Pokopia , you need to smelt one of three raw materials inside a Smelting Furnace : Sand Volcanic Ash Sandstone All three produce Glass when burned, so whichever material you have the most of works fine. That said, Volcanic Ash is by far the most practical option once you reach the right area of the map. Smelting Furnace in Rocky Ridges Where Is the First Smelting Furnace? The first Smelting Furnace you can access sits inside a cave in Rocky Ridges , which you discover during the main quest. This is also where Magmar lives, and that detail matters a lot: Magmar fuels the furnace automatically, so you do not need to worry about finding a separate fire source when you are smelting here. If you do not have Magmar available, any Pokémon with the Burn ability can follow you to the furnace and handle the smelting instead. info Volcanic Ash spawns throughout Rocky Ridges in large quantities, making it the easiest and most abundant input for Glass production at this stage of the game. Magmar powers the furnace What Are the Best Materials to Use for Glass? Here is a quick breakdown of each valid input material and how practical each one is: Material Where to Find It Abundance Notes Volcanic Ash Rocky Ridges (everywhere) High Best early-game option Sand Various locations Moderate Useful if Ash runs low Sandstone Rocky areas Moderate Works but less common than Ash Volcanic Ash wins for early-game Glass production simply because Rocky Ridges is covered in it. You can gather a large stack quickly and smelt it all in one session. danger Smelting takes real time to complete. If you want your Glass faster, you can use the time travel mechanic to skip the wait and collect your finished materials immediately. How Do You Get Your Own Smelting Furnace? You are not locked to the Rocky Ridges furnace forever. Magmar will eventually give you the crafting recipe for your own Smelting Furnace , which means you can build one wherever you set up your base. This opens up Glass production anywhere on the map without needing to trek back to Rocky Ridges every time. Unlock your own furnace recipe What Is Glass Used For in Pokémon Pokopia? Glass serves two main purposes in Pokémon Pokopia : Crafting recipes at your crafting bench that require Glass as an ingredient Pokémon Center rebuilds , where certain structures specifically call for Glass to complete the reconstruction If you are working through rebuild quests, stockpiling Glass early saves a lot of backtracking later. It is worth running a few smelting sessions in Rocky Ridges as soon as you unlock the furnace. warning Do not wait until a rebuild quest demands Glass to start producing it. Smelting takes time, and scrambling for materials mid-quest slows your progress significantly. Glass Crafting Steps Here is the full process from start to finish: Progress through the main quest until you reach Rocky Ridges Locate the cave containing the Smelting Furnace ( Magmar 's location) Collect Volcanic Ash from around Rocky Ridges Place Volcanic Ash (or Sand or Sandstone) into the Smelting Furnace Let Magmar or a Pokémon with the Burn ability ignite the furnace Wait for smelting to finish, or use time travel to speed it up Collect your Glass and head to the crafting bench Once Magmar hands over the Smelting Furnace recipe, you can build your own and skip the Rocky Ridges trip entirely for future batches.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Gold Teeth
description: Gold Teeth in Pokémon Pokopia come from appraising Large Relics with Professor Tangrowth. Learn how to farm them and unlock Feraligatr.
content: Gold Teeth are one of the more confusing items in Pokémon Pokopia 's Bubbly Basin expansion. They don't drop from enemies, they're not sold anywhere, and the game gives you almost no hint about what they're actually for. Here's exactly where to find them and why you need them if you want a complete Bubbly Basin Pokédex. How do you get in Pokémon Pokopia? Gold Teeth are obtained exclusively through Professor Tangrowth 's appraisal system . You bring him Large Relics found in Bubbly Basin, and there's a chance he'll hand back Gold Teeth as the result. The catch: it's not guaranteed. Large Relics can yield several different items when appraised, so you may need to collect and appraise multiple before one turns into Gold Teeth . Tangrowth appraisal screen Where to find Large Relics in Bubbly Basin Large Relics are hidden inside glowing yellow blocks scattered throughout Bubbly Basin. To access them, you need Ditto 's Rock Smash ability . Smash a glowing block and collect whatever's inside. The contents of these blocks are randomized between several possible items: Gold Teeth CDs Slabs for the Mew mural Small Relics Fossils Because the drop is random, the best approach is a systematic sweep of the entire Bubbly Basin area rather than targeting one specific spot. Cover the zone thoroughly, smash every glowing yellow block you find, and bring everything back to Professor Tangrowth . tip Don't ignore blocks in harder-to-reach corners of Bubbly Basin. The glowing yellow blocks can appear at various elevations, so check both ground level and elevated areas. Glowing relic blocks in Bubbly Basin What are used for in Pokémon Pokopia? Gold Teeth serve two purposes. First, they function as a toy item that can be placed in your environment as decoration or used to raise a Pokémon's comfort level. Second, and more importantly, they're a required ingredient for a specific habitat. How to spawn with To add Feraligatr to your Bubbly Basin roster, you need to build the Biteable Punching Bag Habitat . Feraligatr is the only Pokémon that spawns there, making this habitat the sole way to encounter the fully-evolved form of Totodile in Bubbly Basin. The Biteable Punching Bag Habitat requires four items: Loading table... warning Don't accidentally use your Gold Teeth purely as decoration before building the habitat. If you misplace them or use them for comfort bonuses, you'll need to farm more Large Relics before you can spawn Feraligatr . Feraligatr habitat build layout Can you get more if you lose them? Yes. If you've already used your Gold Teeth or need additional copies, you can use the camera and 3D Printer to duplicate the item. This means losing them isn't a permanent setback, but it does add extra steps before you can build the habitat. tip Gold Teeth are classified as a toy in the game's item system, which is why they double as both a comfort item and a habitat ingredient. Keep that in mind when sorting your inventory. How to farm Large Relics efficiently Since the Gold Teeth drop isn't guaranteed, having a reliable relic-farming loop matters. After testing the system across multiple runs, here's what works: Enter Bubbly Basin and locate every glowing yellow block on the map. Use Ditto 's Rock Smash to break each block and collect the contents. Return to Professor Tangrowth and appraise all Large Relics at once. If no Gold Teeth appear, exit, wait for blocks to respawn, and repeat. The other items you collect in the process (CDs, Small Relics, fossils, Mew mural slabs) aren't wasted. Mew mural slabs in particular contribute to another Bubbly Basin unlock, so keep those separate. For a deeper look at what else Bubbly Basin has to offer, the Pokémon Pokopia Bubbly Basin guides cover everything from Ocean Doors to Shiny Pearl farming. Ditto Rock Smash on relic blocks Is worth the effort? For Pokédex completion, yes. Feraligatr has no other spawn point in Bubbly Basin, and the Biteable Punching Bag Habitat is the only way to add it to your roster. If you're working toward a full Bubbly Basin Pokédex, Gold Teeth aren't optional. The habitat itself also only requires Feraligatr , so once it's built and the spawn triggers, you're done with that slot. The grind is front-loaded on the relic farming side, not on the habitat management side. If you're still working through the earlier parts of the expansion, the guide to unlocking Bubbly Basin is a good starting point before you go hunting for relics. And if you want to make the most of your time in the zone, check out the Shiny Pearls farming guide to stack resources while you sweep for glowing blocks.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Hoppip, Skiploom, and Jumpluff
description: Discover how to get Hoppip, Skiploom, and Jumpluff in Pokémon Pokopia during the limited-time event, including their spawn requirements, habitats, and item costs.
content: A limited-time event in Pokémon Pokopia adds three new Pokémon to the island: Hoppip , Skiploom , and Jumpluff . These Pokémon appear during a seasonal event and require specific steps before they can join a player’s Pokédex. Unlike some Pokémon in Pokopia that appear naturally after building habitats, this event introduces a mix of direct spawns and habitat-based attractions . Players must rebuild certain facilities, gather event materials, and construct the correct habitats to unlock each evolution in the Hoppip line. This guide explains how to find Hoppip , how to spawn Skiploom , and the fastest way to attract Jumpluff during the event. How to Get Hoppip in Pokémon Pokopia Hoppip is the first Pokémon introduced during the event and is the easiest to obtain. The “More Spores for Hoppip ” event runs from March 10 at 5:00 AM to March 25 at 4:59 AM (local time) . When players log in during this period, a notification appears saying a Pokémon is the “talk of the town.” That Pokémon is Hoppip . Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Hoppip , Skiploom , and Jumpluff Hoppip can appear in any region of Pokopia , but there is one requirement: the Pokémon Center in that region must already be rebuilt . If a Pokémon Center has not been restored, Hoppip will not spawn there. Once Hoppip appears for the first time, players can permanently host it by building a habitat or assigning it a house. To create a habitat for Hoppip , players need: 4 Dandy Flowers After planting and growing the flowers, the habitat becomes available and Hoppip can be assigned to it. Players can also place Hoppip into an existing house if space is available. How to Get Skiploom in Pokémon Pokopia Skiploom does not spawn automatically like Hoppip . Instead, players must build habitats that attract it during the event. There are two habitats capable of spawning Skiploom . The first option is the Yellow Carpet Habitat , which requires 4 Dandy Flowers . However, Skiploom is only a rare spawn in this environment, meaning it may take a while before it appears. The more reliable method is building the Field-Trip Friends Habitat , which significantly improves the chance of Skiploom spawning. Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Hoppip , Skiploom , and Jumpluff This habitat requires three items: Flower Backpack Hoppip Water Bottle Lunch Box These items are purchased from Hoppip at the Pokémon Center using Cotton Spores , an event currency obtained during the Hoppip event. In total, players need 15 Cotton Spores to buy all the required items. After building the habitat, Skiploom has a much better chance of appearing in the area. How to Get Jumpluff in Pokémon Pokopia Jumpluff works similarly to Skiploom and must be attracted using specific habitats. Technically, Jumpluff can spawn from the Yellow Carpet Habitat , but it is classified as a very rare spawn there. Because of this, players may spend a long time waiting for it to appear. The more effective option is building the Dandelion Lunchtime Habitat . Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Hoppip , Skiploom , and Jumpluff This habitat requires the following items: 1 Dandy Flower 1 Flower Cushion 1 Lunch Box 1 Flowery Table Setting Just like the items used for Skiploom habitats, these are purchased from Hoppip using Cotton Spores . To buy everything needed for the habitat, players must exchange 30 Cotton Spores . Once the habitat is built, Jumpluff can begin appearing in the area. Tips for Catching the Hoppip Evolution Line Because the event is limited-time, players should prioritize gathering Cotton Spores and building habitats early. A good strategy is to unlock Hoppip first , then start collecting spores by interacting with it regularly. Those spores can then be used to purchase the items required for the Skiploom and Jumpluff habitats. It is also helpful to rebuild Pokémon Centers in multiple regions , since Hoppip only appears in areas where the center is active. With the right habitats built and enough Cotton Spores collected, players can obtain the full Hoppip , Skiploom , and Jumpluff evolution line before the event ends.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Ice
description: Ice Blocks are among the rarest materials in Pokémon Pokopia. Here's exactly where to find them and what to build with them.
content: Ice Blocks are one of the most elusive materials in Pokémon Pokopia , and plenty of players finish large chunks of the game without ever stumbling across a single one. That's a problem, because Ice is tied directly to a major end-game build that connects to Pokédex completion. Knowing exactly where to look, and how to set yourself up for a steady supply, saves a lot of frustration later. Where To Find Ice Blocks in Pokémon Pokopia There are exactly two sources of Ice Blocks in the game. One sits in the main world and is available as soon as you unlock a specific area. The other requires visiting a particular Dream Island via Drifloon. Both are worth knowing, since neither alone gives you an unlimited daily supply. Palette Town waterfall cave How Do You Get Ice Blocks in Palette Town? Palette Town holds the single largest deposit of Ice Blocks in the entire game, tucked inside a hidden cave behind a waterfall. Here's how to reach it step by step: Unlock Rock Smash and break the wall to the left of the Withered Wasteland Pokémon Center . Head toward the beach. You'll spot a cave entrance to the right and a broken bridge pathway to the left. Rebuild the bridge on the left to access Palette Town . Once inside Palette Town, look for a small rocky structure visible in the distance from the entrance. Walk toward it, then circle around to the right-hand side until you see a waterfall. A Glow Mushroom glows faintly behind the cascading water . Step through the waterfall into the hidden passage. Follow the path inward until you reach a large chamber packed with Ice Blocks and Crystals . This room contains hundreds of Ice Blocks, making it by far the most abundant source in Pokémon Pokopia . Break as many as you need, and stock up generously since this material is used for one of the game's most demanding builds. How to Get Ice at Rock Peak Dream Island The second source is the Rock Peak Dream Island , accessible through Drifloon's Dream Island system. This island reliably contains a small amount of Ice inside the rocky structure at its centre. To visit this island, you need to bring the correct Doll. Specifically, you need the Clefairy Doll to unlock access to Rock Peak Dream Island. How To Get the Clefairy Doll There are two ways to obtain the Clefairy Doll : Find it randomly from the shiny glowing spots scattered across the ground throughout the game. Purchase it from the Pokémon Center Shop once you have raised Palette Town's Environment Level high enough. Once you arrive at Rock Peak Dream Island, head into the rocky structure at the centre and dig deep. The Ice supply there is smaller than the Palette Town cave, but it refreshes on a daily cycle. danger Dream Islands follow a strict daily limit. You can only visit one Dream Island per day , and resources do not respawn until 5am the following in-game day. If you need Ice faster, time-travelling via the Nintendo Switch 2 system clock is a valid option the game supports. Rock Peak Dream Island select What Is Ice Used For in Pokémon Pokopia? Ice Blocks serve two main purposes in Pokémon Pokopia : Freezing Chambers Kit : This is the primary reason to farm Ice. The Freezing Chambers is one of the game's biggest construction projects, and it's directly tied to Pokédex completion. Without it, finishing the Pokédex is not possible. Habitat and house decoration: Any leftover Ice can be used as a building block to construct homes for Pokémon or to decorate habitats, which contributes to Comfort and Environment Level gains. Because the Freezing Chambers Kit demands a large quantity of Ice and significant cleared space, prioritising your Palette Town cave run early gives you a head start on what is otherwise a late-game bottleneck. Quick Tips for Farming Ice Efficiently Visit Palette Town as soon as you unlock it and clear out the cave completely on your first trip. Bring Hamburger Steaks to maintain stamina during extended mining sessions deep in the cave. Check the Rock Peak Dream Island daily once you have the Clefairy Doll, even if the yield is small. If you're in a hurry, adjusting the in-game time to the next day (5am) resets Dream Island resources without waiting in real time. Save Ice specifically for the Freezing Chambers Kit before spending it on decoration, since the kit is required for full Pokédex completion.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Inflatable Sudowoodo
description: Claim the Inflatable Sudowoodo decoration in Pokémon Pokopia's April Fools event. Here's exactly how to get it in minutes.
content: Pokémon Pokopia is running a one-day April Fools' event on April 1, 2026, and the reward is exactly as absurd as it should be: a dancing Inflatable Sudowoodo decoration for your town. The whole thing takes about two minutes to complete, but there are a couple of prerequisites worth knowing before you log in. What is the April Fools' event in Pokémon Pokopia? The April Fools' Day event is a limited, single-day celebration tied to April 1. The main reward is the Inflatable Sudowoodo , a balloon-style outdoor decoration that stands up and sways around, mimicking the Rock-type Pokémon it's based on. The choice of Sudowoodo is a neat fit: the Pokémon's Japanese name literally translates to "lie" (うそ), and it famously pretends to be a tree to avoid confrontation. An inflatable fake tree for April Fools' Day tracks perfectly. Beyond the decoration, there's a fun town-wide Easter egg running on the same day. Your resident Pokémon will pretend to be other Pokémon throughout April 1, so don't panic if your usual crew looks a little unfamiliar. Inflatable Sudowoodo decoration What do you need before you can participate? There's one hard requirement: you must have rebuilt a Pokémon Center in your town. This is the same prerequisite for every other event in Pokopia , so if you've been playing for any length of time, you almost certainly already have it. The event is not available on Cloud Island, so make sure you're in your main town. danger If you haven't rebuilt your Pokémon Center yet, do that first. Without it, you can't access the PC or the Challenges menu where events live. Here's a quick summary of everything relevant to the event: Detail Info Event name April Fools' Day Date April 1, 2026 (one day only) Reward Inflatable Sudowoodo decoration Requirement Pokémon Center rebuilt in your town Cloud Island Not available Missable? Yes, but recoverable via time travel How do you claim the Inflatable Sudowoodo? Unlike standard event claims, the Inflatable Sudowoodo is earned by participating in a series of "Pokémon Impersonation Quizzes." Check the PC : Head to your Pokémon Center and interact with the PC to activate the April Fools' challenge. Find Impersonators : Look for Pokémon in your town with "..." in speech bubbles above their heads. Correctly Identify 3 Pokémon : Talk to them and guess which Pokémon they are imitating. Pro Tip : Pokémon will only imitate other species that live in their specific region (e.g., Withered Wasteland residents only copy other Withered Wasteland dwellers). Claim Reward : Once you have answered three quizzes correctly, return to the PC Challenges menu to claim your Inflatable Sudowoodo . Can you get more? Yes. Once you've unlocked the initial decoration, you can use the 3D Printer in any Pokémon Center to create duplicates. Each additional Inflatable Sudowoodo costs 2 Rare Pokémetals . What if you missed the event? Missing a one-day event feels rough, but Pokopia runs on your Nintendo Switch 2's system clock, which means you can time travel back to April 1 and claim the item retroactively. Here's how: Save your game and close Pokopia Open System Settings on your Nintendo Switch 2 Go to the Date & Time tab Turn off "Synchronize Clock via Internet" Manually set the date to April 1, 2026 Relaunch Pokémon Pokopia and claim the Inflatable Sudowoodo from the Pokémon Center PC Time traveling in Pokopia doesn't affect your save progress, and you can move forward or backward as needed. Once you've claimed the item, you can re-enable internet clock sync and return to the current date. warning Make sure you save before adjusting the system clock. While time travel is generally safe in Pokopia , saving first is a good habit before any system-level change. Is the Inflatable worth getting? For a free decoration that takes under two minutes to claim, yes. The Inflatable Sudowoodo is the only item in the April Fools' event category, so completing the event means you've got the full set by definition. It's a limited decoration that won't come around again outside of time travel, and the Sudowoodo reference is genuinely clever given the Pokémon's identity as Pokopia 's resident prankster. If you want to stay on top of future limited-time events like this one, you can browse more guides and event coverage to make sure nothing slips past you.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Lumber
description: Learn how to get Lumber in Pokémon Pokopia, including how to find Scyther, collect Small Logs, and process them into Lumber for building and crafting.
content: There are many crafting materials in Pokémon Pokopia , and one that players often overlook early on is Lumber . This resource is required fairly early in the game, especially when rebuilding areas like the Withered Wasteland Pokémon Center . The problem is that the game does not immediately explain how Lumber is made. Players first need to gather another material and use the help of a Pokémon with the right specialty. This guide explains how to get Lumber in Pokémon Pokopia , where to find the required materials, and which Pokémon can help process it. How Lumber Works in Pokémon Pokopia Lumber is not collected directly from the environment. Instead, it is crafted from another material called Small Logs . To convert logs into Lumber , players must bring the logs to a Pokémon that has the Chop Specialty . These Pokémon process the raw wood and turn it into usable building material. One of the earliest Pokémon that can do this is Scyther , which also plays a role in rebuilding early facilities. How to Find Scyther Before players can produce Lumber , they first need to attract Scyther . Scyther appears when a Tree-shaded Tall Grass habitat is built. This setup is simple and can be created early in the game. To make this habitat: Place four Tall Grass tiles near a tree Arrange them in a 2×2 square or around the tree Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Lumber After placing the grass, leave the area for a short time. Scyther should eventually appear. Once Scyther settles in, a yellow speech bubble will appear above its head. Talking to Scyther triggers a small request. Bring two Sturdy Sticks , and Scyther will teach the Cut Transformation , which is needed to gather logs. How to Get Small Logs Small Logs are the main material needed to produce Lumber . These logs can only be collected after unlocking the Cut ability . There are two ways to obtain Small Logs: Cutting piles of wood found around areas like the Withered Wasteland Cutting down trees Cutting healthy green trees usually gives better results. If a tree looks dried out or withered, players can revive it by using Water Gun before cutting it down. A healthy tree tends to produce more logs. Early areas usually contain enough wood piles that players can gather logs without needing to restore trees. How to Turn Small Logs into Lumber Once enough Small Logs are collected, players simply need to bring them to Scyther or another Pokémon with the Chop Specialty. Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Lumber The conversion rate is straightforward: 1 Small Log = 5 Lumber Players can give up to 10 logs at once , which produces 50 Lumber after processing. The process takes time, so it is best to leave the Pokémon working and continue exploring or completing other tasks while the Lumber is being prepared. Pokémon That Can Make Lumber Several Pokémon in Pokémon Pokopia can process logs into Lumber . These Pokémon have the Chop Specialty . Scyther Scizor Pinsir Heracross Excadrill Axew Fraxure Haxorus Crobat Farfetch’d Dartrix Having multiple Chop -type Pokémon can help speed up production if players plan to build a lot. What Lumber Is Used For Lumber is one of the most common crafting materials in Pokémon Pokopia . It is mainly used for building structures, crafting wooden items, and upgrading facilities . Because many recipes require wood, it is a good idea to keep extra Lumber stored in a Storage Chest or inventory. Players who enjoy building habitats and decorations will go through this material quickly. Keeping a steady supply of Small Logs and a working Chop Pokémon ensures that Lumber is always available when needed.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get All Paint
description: Learn how to get every colour of Paint in Pokémon Pokopia, including all Paint recipes and Paint Balloon recipes. Complete guide to customizing furniture with Crush Specialty Pokémon and Smearguru.
content: Paint in Pokémon Pokopia is what allows you to change and customise the colour of any furniture items or decorations. This is great for giving otherwise simple, plain furniture a splash of colour and setting up themed habitats for your Pokémon with matching decor. Before you can customise your furniture, you'll need to grind a little to make all the different colours of paint. Here's everything you need to know about how to get all Paint in Pokopia, including all Paint recipes and Paint Balloon recipes. How to Get Paint in Pokémon Pokopia There are two ways to get Paint in Pokémon Pokopia . Earlier in your playthrough, you'll need Berries and Crush Specialty Pokémon to make Paint for you. Later on, you'll be able to buy Paint directly from shops. Method 1: Crush Berries into Paint This is the primary way to get Paint during the early and mid game. Follow these steps: Collect Berries – Every unique type of Berry can be used to make a type of Paint associated with its colour. For example, Leppa Berries create Red Paint while Pecha Berries create Pink Paint . Find a Crush Specialty Pokémon – Show your Berries to a Pokémon with the Crush Specialty , such as Onix in Withered Wastelands or Conkeldurr in Sparkling Skylands. Method 2: Purchase from Shops Once you upgrade Palette Town to Environment Level 5 , you can buy all colours of Paint directly from the PC Shop. This removes the need to gather Berries. Paint is also available from the Cloud Island shop at Level 5. tip Buying Paint from shops is much faster than farming Berries. Focus on raising your Environment Level in Palette Town to unlock the shop as soon as possible! How to Use Paint: Smearguru & Paint Balloons Once you have Paint, there are two ways to colour your items: Smearguru : Head to Bleak Beach and visit Smearguru . Bring your Paint and the item you wish to customise, and they'll paint it for you. Paint Balloons : Alternatively, take your Paint to a Workbench and craft Paint Balloons .
