title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Paper
description: Learn how to make Paper in Pokémon Pokopia using Recycle Pokémon and Wastepaper, plus where to farm materials fast.
content: Paper might seem like a humble material, but in Pokémon Pokopia it is one of the most sought-after resources for completing major quests and crafting furniture. The catch is that you cannot simply find it lying around. You need the right Pokémon, the right raw material, and a little patience. Here is everything you need to know to get your Paper supply flowing. How Do You Make Paper in Pokémon Pokopia? Making Paper in Pokémon Pokopia follows the same logic as producing other refined materials like Lumber or Bricks. You bring a raw resource to a Pokémon with a specific specialty, and that Pokémon processes it into something more useful. In this case, the raw resource is Wastepaper , and the specialty you need is Recycle . The process is straightforward once everything is in place: Recruit a Pokémon with the Recycle Specialty to your island. Collect Wastepaper from Sparkling Skylands or a Dream Island. Hand the Wastepaper to your Recycle Pokémon and let them process it. Come back after some time to collect your finished Paper . info One piece of Wastepaper converts into two pieces of Paper , so your supply doubles with every batch. Stock up on Wastepaper before starting a big crafting session. Which Pokémon Have the Recycle Specialty? The Recycle Specialty is not especially common, but you will encounter your first Recycle Pokémon earlier than you might expect. Trubbish becomes available during the Bleak Beach storyline, specifically after you build the Trash Collection Site habitat . That habitat requires a Waste Bin (any type), a Sign (any type), and one set of Garbage Bags. All three items can be found near the fountain close to the Bleak Beach Pokémon Center, making this one of the easier habitats to assemble. Here is a quick look at Pokémon confirmed to carry the Recycle Specialty: Pokémon When Available Trubbish Bleak Beach (early game) Beldum Later recruitment Porygon Later recruitment Cinccino Later recruitment Metang Required for Sparkling Skylands quest Garbodor Later recruitment Magnezone Later recruitment Koffing Later recruitment Porygon2 Later recruitment Metagross Later recruitment danger During the Sparkling Skylands main quest "Rebuild the Huge Building!", you will specifically need to recruit a Metang to process Paper . Make sure you have one available before starting that quest chain. Where to Find Wastepaper Wastepaper is the base ingredient for Paper , and knowing where to farm it efficiently saves a lot of time. Sparkling Skylands (Best Source) Sparkling Skylands is the primary farming location for Wastepaper . The grey and purple trash blocks scattered across the first two islands of Sparkling Skylands drop Wastepaper when destroyed. Since this is the final required island in the main story, you will not unlock this farm until later in the game, but once you do, Wastepaper becomes easy to stockpile. Bleak Beach (Secondary Source) Wastepaper can occasionally appear in Bleak Beach as well, either on the ground or from breaking certain objects. The supply here is limited compared to Sparkling Skylands, so treat it as a bonus rather than a reliable farm. Dream Island via Dragonite Doll If you own the Dragonite Doll , you can visit the Sky Dream Island by giving the doll to Drifloon . This Dream Island contains a generous amount of Wastepaper and is worth visiting whenever you need a quick top-up outside of Sparkling Skylands. Smash trash blocks for Wastepaper warning Paper is not accessible until you reach Sparkling Skylands in the main story. If a quest or build requires it before then, you will need to progress the storyline first. What Is Paper Used For in Pokémon Pokopia? Paper serves two main purposes: quest completion and furniture crafting . Quest Requirements Skyland Building 4F during the "Rebuild the Huge Building!" quest in Sparkling Skylands. Challenge 3 during the Team Initiation Challenge. Furniture and Crafting Outside of quests, Paper is a crafting ingredient for: Bookshelves Books Various other furniture and decorative items Paper crafts books and shelves How to Get Paper Early Short answer: not really. Paper production is gated behind reaching Sparkling Skylands because that is where Wastepaper is found in meaningful quantities. You can encounter Trubbish and set up your Recycle operation at Bleak Beach, but without a steady Wastepaper supply, production will be slow. The most efficient approach is to unlock Trubbish at Bleak Beach early so your Recycle infrastructure is ready, then immediately start farming Wastepaper the moment you arrive at Sparkling Skylands. info Build the Trash Collection Site habitat at Bleak Beach as soon as you finish the "Brighten Things Up" quest. Having Trubbish ready means you can start processing Wastepaper the instant you collect any, rather than scrambling to set up the habitat later.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Bubbly Basin Guide: How to Get Phione
description: Get Phione in Pokémon Pokopia Bubbly Basin by visiting the Dream Island with the Starmie Doll. Learn where to find it and what to look for.
content: Phione is one of the trickier Pokémon to add to your Pokédex in Pokémon Pokopia . Unlike the vast majority of Pokémon that show up once you build the right Habitat, Phione skips that whole system entirely. Getting it requires a specific item, a special island, and a healthy amount of patience since luck is genuinely part of the process. What do you need to find in Bubbly Basin? Phione only appears on the Bubbly Basin Dream Island , and the only way to reach that island is by using the Starmie Doll . If you haven't tracked that item down yet, check out our guide on how to find the Starmie Doll in Bubbly Basin before continuing here. Once you have the Starmie Doll, place it somewhere on your island and interact with it. Doing so summons Drifloon , who whisks you off to the Dream Island tied to the doll. That's your gateway to Phione. important Phione is not guaranteed to appear every time you visit. The Dream Island has only a chance of spawning it on any given trip, so you may need multiple visits before you encounter Phione . Check Pokédex on arrival How to check if is actually there Before you spend time combing the entire Dream Island, open your Pokédex the moment you land . Look at the list of entities currently present on the island. If the list shows only you and Drifloon , Phione is not there. Save yourself the search and come back another day. If you see a question mark icon in the list, Phione is present and waiting to be found. This trick saves a lot of wasted exploration. The Dream Island isn't tiny, and hunting every corner for a Pokémon that isn't even there is a frustrating way to spend your daily visit. tip You can only visit the Dream Island once per day. If Phione doesn't show up on your first attempt, you'll have to wait until the next day and try again. Where is 's room on the Dream Island? Phione doesn't roam freely around the island. It sits inside a walled-off brick room that looks noticeably different from everything else on the Dream Island. You're scanning for dark grey and tan brick blocks with solid dark pink blocks used as accents. That color combination stands out sharply against the rest of the environment. The exact position of this room changes between visits, so there's no fixed map coordinate to follow. What stays consistent is the room's appearance. Once you've seen it once, you'll recognize it immediately on future trips. The room tends to appear deep inside underwater caves on the island. Occasionally rocks block the entrance, requiring the Rock Smash ability to clear the path. Other times the room sits in plain sight with nothing blocking access. Either way, the outer structure always looks the same, so keep scanning your surroundings as you move through the island. warning Don't skip the Pokédex check when you land. Spending time breaking rocks and exploring caves only to discover Phione wasn't spawned that day is a real time sink . Loading table... What happens when you find ? Once you locate the brick room and enter it, a cutscene plays automatically . Phione speaks to you and asks if you can help it find a new place to live. Agreeing brings Phione back to your island, officially adding it to your Pokédex. There's no battle, no complex interaction sequence. The whole thing resolves through conversation, which makes the actual encounter feel rewarding after however many days it took to get Phione to spawn. Phione asks to move in What should you do after getting ? With Phione secured, there's still plenty left to do in Bubbly Basin. title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Pokémetal
description: Learn how to get Pokémetal in Pokémon Pokopia, including fragments, furnace smelting, trading methods, and where to find Rare Pokémetal.
content: Pokémetal is one of the rarest crafting materials in Pokémon Pokopia . This rainbow-colored metal is used in several late-game recipes, rebuilding projects, and special machines like the 3D Printer. Because Pokémetal does not appear as often as other resources, players will want to know every reliable way to collect it. This guide explains how to get Pokémetal, where to find Pokémetal Fragments, how to smelt them, and what Pokémetal is used for later in the game. How to Get Pokémetal There are several ways to obtain Pokémetal in Pokémon Pokopia. Players can either find Pokémetal Ingots directly or gather Pokémetal Fragments and turn them into ingots using a Furnace. Buy Pokémetal from the Pokémon Center Shop One of the easiest ways to get Pokémetal is by checking the Pokémon Center PC shop . These ingots sometimes appear as shop items, especially in areas like the Withered Wasteland . They usually cost a good amount of Life Coins , but this currency becomes easier to earn as players progress. Whenever Pokémetal appears in the shop—whether as a daily item or an environment reward—it is usually worth buying. Find Pokémetal While Exploring Players should always check the Poké Ball items scattered around each map . These collectibles can contain many things such as materials, furniture, or crafting recipes, and sometimes they also contain Pokémetal Ingots. One early example can be found in the Withered Wasteland , near the area where players first meet Professor Tangrowth . Behind some vines, there is a small hidden spot that contains several Pokémetal pieces. Using the Cut Transformation clears the vines and allows players to collect the items. Exploring thoroughly and collecting every Poké Ball item is one of the best ways to build a stockpile of Pokémetal early in the game. Trade with Pokémon Vendors Another reliable method unlocks later when players have a Pokémon with the Trade Specialty . After building a Pokémon Center or placing a Cash Register , that Pokémon can open a small shop and trade items with the player. Pokémetal sometimes appears in these trades. However, trades usually require items worth around 1,000 value . Because of this, it helps to bring plenty of common items. Crops work well since each crop typically has a value of around 50 , making them an easy way to reach the required trade amount. How to Get Pokémetal Fragments Besides ingots, players can also collect Pokémetal Fragments , which are used to craft Pokémetal. Fragments appear in special blocks that can be broken with the Rock Smash Transformation . To activate this ability at full strength, players need to eat a Hamburger Steak before breaking the blocks. Some places where Pokémetal Fragment Blocks appear include: Dream Islands accessed using the Dragonite Doll The Sparkling Skylands Small caves and hidden areas around floating islands These blocks are not extremely common, but checking these areas regularly can provide a steady supply of fragments. How to Smelt Pokémetal Once players collect Poké metal Fragments , they need to convert them into ingots. This is done using a Furnace . To operate the furnace, players must assign a Pokémon with the Burn Specialty . That Pokémon will process the fragments and smelt them into usable Pokémetal Ingots , which can then be used in crafting recipes and building projects. What Pokémetal Is Used For Pokémetal is mainly used for advanced crafting and rebuilding projects . Several appliance-themed recipes require it, including items like: Washing Machine Fridge Game Boy These objects are needed to complete certain progression challenges, including the Team Initiation Challenge . Pokémetal is also used to rebuild structures such as the Sparkling Skylands Pokémon Center and other large building blueprints. One of the most important uses is the 3D Printer , which becomes available in rebuilt Pokémon Centers. The 3D Printer allows players to duplicate items shown in photos they capture. This makes it possible to reproduce rare collectibles, but each copy costs a small amount of Pokémetal. What Is Rare Pokémetal Rare Pokémetal is an upgraded version of the normal material. It is much harder to obtain and only appears occasionally. Players have a small chance to receive Rare Pokémetal when breaking Pokémetal Fragment Blocks. Because the drop rate is low, collecting enough usually takes time. Rare Pokémetal Uses Rare Pokémetal is required for a few special late-game recipes. Players will need it to craft the following items: Tidal Bell Transparent Bell Each recipe requires five Rare Pokémetal , meaning players need ten total to craft both items. Rare Pokémetal is also required when using the 3D Printer to duplicate certain rare objects such as unique flowers or special berry trees. Final Tips for Farming Pokémetal Since Pokémetal is uncommon, players should collect it whenever they see it. Checking shops regularly, exploring maps thoroughly, and farming fragments from Dream Islands will slowly build a strong supply. Once players unlock the Furnace and the 3D Printer , Pokémetal becomes one of the most important materials in Pokémon Pokopia’s late game progression.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Portal Pods
description: Get Portal Pods in Pokémon Pokopia fast. Find the free one in Bubbly Basin or unlock the craft recipe via Palette Town.
content: Pokémon Pokopia added Portal Pods with its 2.0.0 update, and they solve one of the game's most persistent headaches: running out of accessible storage mid-session. Think of them as the Pokopia equivalent of Minecraft's Ender Chest. Each Portal Pod holds up to 140 stacks of items, and any Portal Pod you interact with anywhere in the world taps into that same shared inventory. Place one at your base, one in the field, and your items follow you everywhere. There are two ways to get one: find the free copy hidden in Bubbly Basin, or unlock the crafting recipe by progressing through Palette Town. Here's exactly how both work. Portal Pod holds 140 item stacks Where to find the free Portal Pod in Bubbly Basin The quickest way to get your first Portal Pod requires the Expansion Pass and access to Bubbly Basin . If you have both, this is the route to take before spending anything on crafting. From the Bubbly Basin entrance, move past the opening area where Popplio first guides you. Rather than swimming underwater the whole way, use Surf to travel above the water 's surface. Head past the ornate building that pokes above the waterline, and aim for the island directly behind it. tip Navigating above water with Surf is faster than diving through the underwater sections. Save the diving for when you reach the island. Once you reach that island, dive beneath the surface and enter the building. Inside, you'll find a Portal Pod that can be collected using Rock Smash . There's a second one at the bottom of the stairs at the back of the building, sitting inside a Poké Ball. That gives you two Portal Pods from a single trip. How to get more Portal Pods after the first two Two Portal Pods is a solid start, but you'll likely want more as your base and travel routes expand. There are two methods to duplicate them without crafting. First, once you have a Portal Pod in hand, head to the 3D printer inside a rebuilt Pokémon Center . Take a picture of the Portal Pod, and you can print as many copies as you want from that point forward. If you haven't rebuilt yours yet, check out the Pokémon Pokopia guide on rebuilding the Pokémon Center to get that structure up and running. Second, if a friend has a Portal Pod on their island, you can travel there and photograph theirs instead. The same applies to any Cloud Island you visit. Either way, the photo is what unlocks the print option, so the source doesn't matter. important The 3D printer method only works after the Pokémon Center has been rebuilt. If yours isn't ready yet, the Bubbly Basin find is your only immediate option. How to unlock the Portal Pod crafting recipe Crafting a Portal Pod from scratch is the alternative path, and it doesn't require the Expansion Pass. The catch is that it takes longer to unlock. Palette Town is where the recipe comes from. This separate area functions as a blank building canvas where you can encounter Pokémon not found in the four main towns or in Bubbly Basin. As you build and develop Palette Town, your environment level increases, and leveling it up enough after the 2.0.0 update rewards you with the Portal Pod recipe. Loading table... The crafting route is described as the cheapest option long-term since you skip the 3D printer 's material costs entirely. If you're patient and already working through Palette Town progression, it's worth holding out for the recipe rather than spending resources on printing. warning Don't assume the crafting recipe is available from the start of Palette Town. You need to reach a specific environment level threshold, so build consistently and check your rewards as you progress. Palette Town unlocks the recipe What makes Portal Pods worth the effort? The 140-stack shared inventory is the headline, but the real value is the flexibility. Once you have Portal Pods placed at multiple locations, you stop making trips back to base just to deposit materials. Combined with smart fast travel options in Pokémon Pokopia , Portal Pods cut out a significant chunk of the back-and-forth that slows down building sessions. For players deep into crafting, having access to your full material stockpile from anywhere on the island changes how you plan builds. You can gather resources in one area and immediately start constructing in another without ever unloading at a chest first. Place Portal Pods at every base If you're still building out your island and figuring out which materials to prioritize, the best items to buy first in Pokémon Pokopia is a good starting point before committing your resources. title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Shiny Pearls in Bubbly Basin
description: Shiny Pearls are essential for Bubbly Basin progress in Pokémon Pokopia. Learn which Pokémon have the Scrub ability and how to farm them fast.
content: Shiny Pearls are one of the most-needed resources in Pokémon Pokopia 's Bubbly Basin expansion, and the game does a poor job of telling you how to actually get them. You won't find them sitting on the ocean floor. Getting them requires a specific Pokémon ability, and if you don't know which one, you'll be sitting on a pile of useless Grubby Pearls wondering what went wrong. What are Shiny Pearls and why do you need them? Shiny Pearls are a refined material used in a wide range of crafting recipes and Pokémon requests throughout Bubbly Basin. As you rebuild Cerulean City, demand for Shiny Pearls ramps up fast, and running dry on them will stall your progress significantly. The raw form , Grubby Pearls , are plentiful in Bubbly Basin and easy to collect. The problem is they have zero direct use on their own. Every Grubby Pearl needs to be converted into a Shiny Pearl before it becomes useful, and that conversion process is the part most players miss. Grubby Pearls before conversion How do you get Shiny Pearls in Pokémon Pokopia? Shiny Pearls cannot be found directly in the overworld. The only way to produce them is by assigning a Pokémon with the Scrub specialty to process your Grubby Pearls. Without a Scrub Pokémon in your setup, those Grubby Pearls will sit in your inventory forever. The first time most players encounter this mechanic is through a request from Mareanie , who asks for a Shiny Pearl. That request effectively serves as the game's tutorial for the system, pointing you toward Cloyster as the most accessible Scrub Pokémon at that stage. tip Check your active requests regularly. Mareanie 's Shiny Pearl request is the clearest early-game signal that you need to set up a Scrub Pokémon as soon as possible. How to get for the Scrub specialty Cloyster is the easiest entry point for the Scrub specialty in Bubbly Basin. It spawns from the Swaying Flower Bed & Seaweed Habitat , which you can build yourself once you know the recipe. The habitat requires: 4x Seabad Flowers 1x Chimney Rock 2x Lush Seaweed Once the habitat is placed and Cloyster spawns, you can assign it to process Grubby Pearls into Shiny Pearls. The habitat requirements are revealed as part of Mareanie 's request, so following that quest line is the most natural path to unlocking this conversion chain. Cloyster habitat build requirements All Pokémon with the Scrub specialty Cloyster isn't the only option. Two other Pokémon also carry the Scrub specialty, and running multiple Scrub Pokémon simultaneously is the fastest way to process a large Grubby Pearl backlog. Loading table... Splitting a large stack of Grubby Pearls across Cloyster , Shellder , and Sharpedo at the same time cuts down the wait considerably compared to routing everything through a single Pokémon. warning Don't let Grubby Pearls pile up without a Scrub Pokémon assigned. A large backlog takes time to clear, and many crafting recipes and requests will be blocked until you have enough Shiny Pearls converted. Tips for keeping your Shiny Pearl supply healthy The crafting demand for Shiny Pearls in Bubbly Basin is consistent enough that running out is a genuine problem if you're not proactive. A few habits that help: Keep track of where your Scrub Pokémon are located at all times so you can assign them quickly when a batch of Grubby Pearls comes in. Build multiple Scrub-compatible habitats if you want a faster pipeline. Having Shellder and Sharpedo alongside Cloyster means you're never bottlenecked by a single Pokémon. Prioritize Grubby Pearl collection during your regular Bubbly Basin sessions so your Scrub Pokémon always have material to work with. tip Grubby Pearls are found throughout Bubbly Basin and are one of the more common drops in the area, so supply on the raw material side shouldn't be the problem. The conversion rate is the bottleneck. Assigning Cloyster to Scrub tasks What else should you know about Bubbly Basin? Shiny Pearls are just one piece of the Bubbly Basin resource puzzle. title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Learn Suck and Move Water
description: Learn how to unlock the Suck move in Pokémon Pokopia to transfer water, clear floods, and build custom ponds on your island.
content: If you have been trying to move water around in Pokémon Pokopia and keep hitting a wall, you are not alone. The Suck move is one of Ditto 's most useful abilities in the game, letting you vacuum up bodies of water and deposit them exactly where you want. But unlocking it requires working through a specific chain of story events that the game does not spell out clearly. Here is everything you need to know to get Suck and start reshaping your island's waterways. What Does the Suck Move Actually Do? Suck functions like a water bucket in sandbox games such as Minecraft . It allows Ditto to inhale a block of liquid and carry it until you choose to release it somewhere else. According to game guides, the move works on a wide range of liquids including water , ocean water , hot-spring water , vending machine drinks , and even lava . This makes it one of the most flexible tools in Pokémon Pokopia for island customization. You can use it to: Clear flooded areas that are blocking habitats Construct custom ponds, creeks, or rivers from scratch Redirect water sources to attract water -type Pokémon Build hot springs or lava features for specific habitat requirements Ditto 's Suck move in action warning Spitting liquid onto an area that is not enclosed by blocks will cause it to spread unevenly. This can accidentally flood nearby habitats, so always prepare a contained pool before releasing liquid. How to Unlock the Suck Move Unlocking Suck is tied to a specific questline and cannot be obtained by exploring freely. You need to follow the story progression carefully across two separate areas. Step 1: Rebuild the Rocky Ridges Pokémon Center Before anything else, you must advance far enough through the Rocky Ridges area to rebuild the Pokémon Center there. This is a major milestone that sits at the end of a series of smaller quests and tasks in that zone. Expect to spend a significant amount of time completing those prerequisite requests before the center becomes available. As confirmed by community discussion on Reddit and summarized across multiple guides, the Rocky Ridges Pokémon Center rebuild is the key gate that unlocks the next step in the chain. Step 2: Talk to Piplup at Bleak Beach Once the Rocky Ridges Pokémon Center is rebuilt, head to Bleak Beach and speak directly with Piplup . This step is easy to miss because the request does not appear in your request list automatically. You must physically talk to Piplup to trigger the Make a Waterfall request. danger Do not wait for this quest to appear on its own. It only activates after a direct conversation with Piplup , so make the trip to Bleak Beach as soon as the Pokémon Center is done. Step 3: Create a Marshy Tall Grass Habitat Piplup 's waterfall request requires the help of Paldean Wooper , who you need to attract to your island. To do this, you must build a marshy tall grass habitat. According to Game8's walkthrough team, this habitat requires placing 4 yellow tall grass tiles adjacent to a body of muddy water . A waterfall of muddy water can be found southwest of the Withered Wasteland gate if you need a source. Once you place the habitat components correctly, wait for Paldean Wooper to arrive. After it shows up and you complete the interaction, Ditto will learn the Suck move. How to Use Suck: Full Controls Once Ditto has learned Suck , using it is straightforward once you understand the button layout. Here is a full breakdown of the controls: Action Button Input Inhale liquid Hold Y + ZR while facing the liquid Spit out liquid Press A while facing target area Gulp and discard liquid Press B to swallow and remove the liquid To pick up water , stand in front of any body of liquid and hold Y while pressing ZR . Ditto will inhale the liquid and hold it. Move to your target location, face the area you want to fill, and press A to release it. info Always build an enclosed pool before spitting out liquid. Any area surrounded by blocks on all sides will contain the liquid neatly. Open terrain will let it spread in unpredictable directions. If you accidentally inhale liquid you do not want to place anywhere, pressing B will make Ditto swallow and permanently discard it. Be careful with this option if your island has limited water sources, since discarded liquid is gone for good. What Liquids Can Suck Move? Suck is not limited to plain water . The full list of transferable liquids in Pokémon Pokopia includes: Water (standard) Ocean water Hot-spring water Vending machine drinks Lava Muddy water This variety opens up a lot of creative possibilities. Moving hot-spring water lets you build custom spa habitats, while relocating lava can help create volcanic terrain features. Why Is the Suck Move Worth the Wait? Unlocking Suck opens up a major layer of island customization that is simply not possible before you have it. Water -type habitats require specific liquid conditions, and being able to relocate water precisely means you can attract Pokémon that would otherwise never appear on your island. Clearing flooded zones also frees up building space that was previously unusable. The progression gate (rebuilding the Rocky Ridges Pokémon Center) takes time, but every step leading up to it also builds out your island in meaningful ways. By the time Paldean Wooper teaches Ditto the move, you will already have a much more developed island to experiment with. For more tips on building habitats, managing island resources, and mastering Ditto 's full move set, browse the latest Pokémon Pokopia guides to keep your island growing.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Make a Bubbly Basin Habitat Warmer
description: Learn how to warm up Bubbly Basin habitats in Pokémon Pokopia. Find the Heat Rock location and all other ways to get one.
content: Pokémon in the underwater Bubbly Basin area of Pokémon Pokopia have different comfort needs than anything you dealt with on the surface, and one of the first requests you'll run into is a Pokémon asking you to make their home warmer. The solution is simpler than you might expect, but finding the right item does require knowing where to look. What is the best way to warm up a Bubbly Basin habitat? A Heat Rock is the item you need. It radiates heat to the surrounding area, making it the go-to fix for any Pokémon complaining about a cold habitat in Bubbly Basin. Place it in the habitat and the temperature issue resolves. The Heat Rock belongs to a set of four special rocks in Pokémon Pokopia, each designed to modify the local environment in different ways. Loading table... All four are rare items, so you will not stumble across them constantly. The Heat Rock is the one to prioritize for warming up any Bubbly Basin habitat. tip Each special rock affects only the area nearby, so placement matters. Put the Heat Rock directly inside the habitat that needs warming rather than leaving it somewhere else in Bubbly Basin. Bubbly Basin cave entrance Where to find a in Bubbly Basin The most straightforward way to get a Heat Rock is to grab the one sitting inside a Pokéball in a cave within Bubbly Basin. From the gate entrance, head into the main area where Popplio first guides you. Look for a cave on the right side of the stairs — it has black stone above the entrance and scaffolding pieces at the front. Head toward the back of that cave and you will find a Pokéball containing a Heat Rock . That is the one guaranteed spawn, so if you have not collected it yet, that is your fastest route. Heat Rock Pokéball location What are the other ways to get a ? Once you have found your first Heat Rock , there are a couple of ways to get more. 3D Printer : Take a photo of the Heat Rock you already own, then use the 3D Printer to create a duplicate. This costs resources, including Poké Ingots , which are not cheap, so plan accordingly. Cloud Islands: If you have not found the cave Heat Rock yet, some Cloud Islands carry one. Traveling to a Cloud Island that has one lets you collect it without needing the cave first. Gimmighoul and Gholdengo trades: Trading with these two Pokémon can yield a Heat Rock as a reward. The item pool for these trades is broad, though, so this method is not reliable as your primary approach. warning Duplicating items via the 3D Printer requires Poké Ingots, which are a costly resource. Save duplication for items you genuinely need multiples of rather than burning Ingots early. For players managing habitat comfort across multiple Pokémon, knowing how to increase Comfort Level more broadly will help you stay ahead of requests like this one. 3D Printer duplication menu How does the fit into Bubbly Basin habitat management? Bubbly Basin sits underwater, which changes the rules for several comfort mechanics that work fine on the surface. Temperature control through the Heat Rock is one of the adjustments the DLC introduces specifically for this environment. If you are also dealing with humidity-related requests from your Pokémon, the approach there is different. Check out the guide on how to increase humidity in Pokémon Pokopia to handle those separately. You need the Expansion Pass active to access this area and its unique habitat mechanics. title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Make a Hot-Spring Shower and Get Psyduck
description: Learn how to make a Hot-Spring Shower habitat in Pokémon Pokopia and unlock Psyduck spawns. This guide explains Hot-Spring Water, required items, and the fastest setup.
content: Psyduck is one of the Pokémon players often want to find early in Pokémon Pokopia , but it is not available right away. Unlike some Pokémon that appear naturally during exploration, Psyduck requires a specific habitat setup before it can spawn. This guide explains how to unlock Psyduck , how to build the Hot-Spring Shower habitat , and how to get Hot-Spring Water , which is the key material needed for the environment. When Psyduck Becomes Available Players cannot encounter Psyduck at the very beginning of Pokémon Pokopia. The game first requires progress through the early area of the island. After exploring the first region and unlocking additional building tools and terraforming options, the conditions needed for Psyduck become available. At that point, players can begin building the habitat required to attract it. Psyduck only appears in one specific environment type called the Hot-Spring Shower habitat , which must be created manually. How to Build a Hot-Spring Shower Habitat The Hot-Spring Shower is the only habitat in Pokémon Pokopia that adds Psyduck and Golduck to the Pokémon encounter pool. Psyduck is usually the more common spawn between the two. To create the habitat, players must place the following items together in the same area: One Shower One Seat (any seat works) Two tiles of Hot-Spring Water Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Make a Hot-Spring Shower and Get Psyduck Once these elements are placed close to each other, the environment counts as a Hot-Spring Shower habitat and Psyduck can begin appearing. A simple way to build this setup is inside the Rocky Ridges region. Caves in this area naturally contain Hot-Spring Water, which means players only need to add a Shower and a Seat to complete the habitat. This is usually the fastest method if the goal is to unlock Psyduck quickly. How to Get Hot-Spring Water Hot-Spring Water is one of several liquid types players can place in the environment while terraforming in Pokémon Pokopia. There are two main ways to obtain it. The first method is by collecting natural Hot-Spring Water from areas where it already exists, such as caves in Rocky Ridges. Players can absorb the liquid and place it elsewhere once the proper ability is unlocked. Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Make a Hot-Spring Shower and Get Psyduck The second method involves using an item called Roserade Tea . Roserade Tea can be obtained from a powered Vending Machine . The machine can be used once per day and gives a random item, which may include Fresh Water or Roserade Tea. After drinking Roserade Tea , the player's Ditto temporarily stores liquid. This allows players to place Hot-Spring Water tiles wherever they want, letting them build the Hot-Spring Shower habitat in almost any location. How to Unlock the Liquid Absorb Ability If players want to collect water directly from the environment instead of relying on vending machine items, they must unlock a special ability. This ability comes from Wooper . To start the process, players need to speak with Piplup , who gives a request involving the creation of a Waterfall . Completing this task leads to an interaction with Wooper , which teaches the player how to absorb and store liquids. Once unlocked, this ability greatly expands terraforming options and makes it easier to move Hot-Spring Water from one location to another. Final Tips for Finding Psyduck Once the Hot-Spring Shower habitat is built, Psyduck can begin appearing in the area. If it does not show up immediately, players may need to leave the area and return to refresh Pokémon spawns. Building the habitat in a location that is easy to revisit can make this process faster. Because the habitat also allows Golduck to appear, players can potentially encounter both Pokémon in the same location after the setup is complete.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Make a Pikachu Corner and Unlock Mimikyu
description: Learn how to build a Pikachu Corner in Pokémon Pokopia and attract Mimikyu, including where to find the Pikachu Sofa and Pikachu Doll.
content: Some Pokémon in Pokémon Pokopia appear naturally while exploring the island, but others only show up after players build very specific habitats. One of the most wanted examples is Mimikyu , the Ghost/Fairy Pokémon that disguises itself as Pikachu. Getting Mimikyu is not complicated, but it requires setting up a special habitat called the Pikachu Corner . This guide explains exactly how to build the habitat and where to find the items needed to unlock it. How to Make a Corner The Pikachu Corner is a simple habitat that attracts only one Pokémon: Mimikyu . No other Pokémon can spawn from it, and Mimikyu will not appear through any other habitat in the game. To create the Pikachu Corner, players only need to place two decorations next to each other: Pikachu Sofa Pikachu Doll Place both items side-by-side in your area. After a short period of time, the environment will trigger the habitat effect and Mimikyu will appear nearby . The build itself is easy. The main challenge is unlocking the two Pikachu -themed items required for the habitat. Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Make a Pikachu Corner and Unlock Mimikyu How to Get the The Pikachu Doll can be purchased later through the Pokémon Center PC once it becomes available, but the fastest way to obtain it is by exploring. Players can find one in the Bleak Beach region. Head toward the southern section of the area where an abandoned house sits on a small island. If the player has already encountered Lapras and unlocked the ability to transform into it, reaching the island becomes much easier. Lapras allows safe travel across the water surrounding Bleak Beach. Without Lapras , it is still possible to reach the island by carefully placing blocks to create a path. However, falling into the water will reset progress, so it requires careful movement. Inside the abandoned house, players will find the Pikachu Doll waiting to be collected. How to Get the The Pikachu Sofa is also located in the Bleak Beach area, but this one is hidden inside the ruins of the S.S. Anne ship. Unlike the Pikachu Doll , this item is much harder to reach without Lapras . The ship is surrounded by water , so transforming into Lapras is strongly recommended before attempting the trip. Once inside the S.S. Anne, explore the upper levels of the ship until reaching the area with the steering wheel . Nearby, there is a ladder positioned above two bookcases. To reach it: Place a block near the bookcases. Jump onto the top of the shelves. Climb the ladder above them. At the top, players will find a glowing yellow Poké Ball containing the Pikachu Sofa . Some later areas in Pokopia also feature a Pikachu Sofa already placed in the environment, but finding the one inside the S.S. Anne is the earliest way to unlock the Pikachu Corner. How to Spawn Once both items are collected, building the habitat is quick. Simply place the Pikachu Sofa and Pikachu Doll next to each other to form the Pikachu Corner . After a short wait, Mimikyu will appear in the area . Because this Pokémon only spawns from this specific habitat, building the Pikachu Corner is the only reliable way to encounter it. For players trying to complete their Pokopia Pokémon collection, setting up this habitat early is the best strategy to secure Mimikyu as soon as possible.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Make Duckweed
description: Discover how to make Duckweed in Pokémon Pokopia using Leafage, how to unlock it with Salad, and how Duckweed habitats attract Pokémon like Lotad.
content: Duckweed is one of the environmental elements players will need to understand in Pokémon Pokopia . This floating plant grows on water and is required for certain Habitats that attract specific Pokémon. Players who want to complete the Pokopia Pokédex will eventually need to create Duckweed , since some Pokémon only appear in habitats that require it. Learning how to generate it early makes building habitats and unlocking new Pokémon much easier. This guide explains how to make Duckweed in Pokémon Pokopia and whether it can be moved after being placed. How to Make Duckweed In Pokémon Pokopia , Duckweed is created using the Leafage ability while it is powered up. However, Leafage cannot produce Duckweed immediately at the start of the game. The ability first needs to be enhanced by eating a Salad . Players who have not unlocked cooking yet should head to Rocky Ridges and rescue Chef Dente . After helping him, cooking becomes available and salads can be prepared. Once a Salad is eaten, the Leafage PP bar turns yellow , showing that the ability is powered up and has a limited number of enhanced uses. Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Make Duckweed After powering up Leafage, creating Duckweed is easy: Go to any body of water Use the Leafage ability on the water surface Hold the ability button to create a larger Duckweed patch Larger patches of Duckweed will trigger the Uplifting Duckweed Habitat , which allows Pokémon like Lotad and its evolution line to appear. Because of this, many players use Duckweed mainly for habitat creation and Pokémon spawns. Can You Move Duckweed? Currently, Duckweed cannot be moved once it has been placed in Pokémon Pokopia. Abilities that work on other environmental objects do not relocate it: Rototiller does not pick it up Cut only destroys the Duckweed and leaves behind collectible Leaves Because of this limitation, the best approach when building habitats is to create more Duckweed than needed and then trim the extra areas using Cut. Fortunately, most Duckweed -based habitats in the game do not require extremely precise placement, so adjusting the shape is usually enough to complete the setup. Why Duckweed Is Important Duckweed plays a key role in several habitat builds in Pokémon Pokopia. Some Pokémon will only spawn in environments that contain floating foliage, making it necessary for Pokédex completion. Once players unlock cooking, power up Leafage with Salad, and start placing Duckweed in water areas, they can begin unlocking the Uplifting Duckweed Habitat and attract Pokémon such as Lotad, Lombre, and Ludicolo . For players focusing on habitat creation and rare Pokémon spawns, mastering Duckweed placement is an important step in progressing through the game.

title: Pokémon Pokopia: How to Make Lava Pools and Streams
description: Learn how to make Lava pools, streams, and waterfalls in Pokémon Pokopia, how to get Chili Sauce, and how to remove or stop Lava from spreading.
content: Lava is one of the more unique environmental liquids players can work with in Pokémon Pokopia . While Lava naturally appears in certain areas of the map, players can also create their own Lava pools, streams, and waterfalls for custom terrain builds. However, Lava works differently from other liquids in the game. Unlike Hot Spring Water or Muddy Water , it cannot be safely collected directly by jumping into it. Because of that, players need a different method if they want to use Lava for building or terraforming. Here’s how to make Lava in Pokémon Pokopia and how to remove or control it when needed. How to Make Lava in Pokémon Pokopia The easiest and safest way to create Lava is by using Chili Sauce . In Pokémon Pokopia, Ditto can absorb different liquid types. When Ditto consumes Chili Sauce , it temporarily fills with Lava. Players can then place that Lava anywhere in the environment to create custom features like pools, streams, or waterfalls. Pokémon Pokopia: How to Make Lava Pools and Streams The Lava behaves like other liquids in the game and will naturally flow across terrain depending on the layout of the ground. Trying to absorb Lava directly from the environment is not recommended. Jumping into Lava damages Ditto , and repeated attempts will cause the character to respawn nearby. Because of this, Chili Sauce is the intended method for using Lava in builds. How to Get Chili Sauce can be obtained from Vending Machines found around Pokopia. These machines require electricity and will dispense one random item per day when interacted with. Chili Sauce is one of the possible rewards, but the item given is completely random. Since there is no way to guarantee Chili Sauce from a single machine, players should interact with as many Vending Machines as possible each day. Saving the items received can also help build up a supply of liquids for future building projects. How Lava Works When Placed Once Lava is placed in the environment, it behaves like a flowing liquid. This means players can design different terrain features such as: Lava pools Lava streams Lava waterfalls Because Lava flows naturally across terrain, shaping the land beforehand helps control where the Lava spreads. This makes it useful for creating themed areas, especially habitats suited for Fire-type Pokémon , where Lava environments match the overall aesthetic. Can You Move Lava in Pokémon Pokopia? Lava cannot be picked up or moved once it has been placed. Unlike some other liquids in the game, there is no mechanic that allows players to collect placed Lava again. However, it is still possible to remove it from the environment. How to Remove Lava To remove Lava, players need to use Water Spray . Spraying water on Lava converts the liquid into a solid rock block . Once the Lava has turned into rock, it can be destroyed using Rock Smash . This method allows players to clean up mistakes or reshape Lava environments. If the entire Lava area is converted into rock, the Lava will stop appearing in that location. Blocking the Lava source will also prevent it from spreading further. Tips for Building Lava Areas Players who want to build Lava landscapes should prepare the terrain first before placing the liquid. This helps control how far the Lava flows and makes it easier to design streams or pools. Saving Chili Sauce bottles from Vending Machines is also useful since Lava creation depends on having them available. With the right setup, players can design their own volcanic-style zones in Pokémon Pokopia, which work well for Fire-type habitats or themed environments.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Unlock Bubbly Basin
description: Learn how to unlock Bubbly Basin in Pokémon Pokopia. Complete every prerequisite, find Popplio, and dive into the DLC with this step-by-step guide.
content: The Bubbly Basin DLC is finally live in Pokémon Pokopia , and it brings the first wave of paid Expansion Pass content to the game. Getting in requires a few steps that the game doesn't spell out clearly, so if you've bought the pass and can't figure out why Bubbly Basin isn't showing up yet, here's exactly what you need to do. What are the prerequisites to unlock Bubbly Basin? Bubbly Basin isn't accessible from the start, and the gate won't open until you've met every requirement. Work through this list before expecting anything to happen. Progress requirements You need to have moved past the starting area of the game before Bubbly Basin becomes relevant. Specifically: Complete the Withered Wasteland area, which is where Pokopia begins. Unlock access to Bleak Beach . Finish the 'Raise the Environment Level in Bleak Beach' request. That last one is the gating condition most players miss. You can own the Expansion Pass and have all three movement abilities and still find nothing if that request isn't done. Bleak Beach Pokémon Center Ability requirements Three movement abilities are required to reach and enter Bubbly Basin: Loading table... If you've already raised the Bleak Beach environment level, Jump and Surf are almost certainly already in your toolkit. Dive is the new one added in the v2.0.0 update, and you'll need to learn it from Manaphy specifically. important Dive is the final unlock that triggers Popplio 's appearance. Without it, nothing happens at the Pokémon Center on Bleak Beach. Expansion Pass requirement The Expansion Pass must be purchased. This is the only paid requirement in the list, but it's non-negotiable. Popplio will not appear at Bleak Beach without it , regardless of how far you've progressed in the base game. How to start the Bubbly Basin DLC Once every prerequisite is ticked off, head to the Pokémon Center on Bleak Beach . You'll find Popplio waiting there. Start a conversation with it, and Popplio will talk about its home, then point you toward the gate that leads to Bubbly Basin. The gate itself sits beneath the surface of the sea, parallel to the back of the Pokémon Center. You'll need Dive to reach it, which is why learning the ability from Manaphy first is required. tip If you lose track of where the gate is, talk to Popplio again and it will show you the way. Look for furniture and decorations scattered across the seabed as visual markers pointing toward the entrance. Popplio guides you to the gate Where exactly is the Bubbly Basin gate? The gate is underwater, directly behind the Pokémon Center on Bleak Beach. Dive down from that position and follow the seabed decorations. The layout uses scattered furniture as a breadcrumb trail, so if you see items on the ocean floor, you're heading in the right direction. After testing the path a few times, the most reliable approach is to dive directly behind the center rather than from the sides. The decorations on the seafloor make it hard to get lost once you're in the water . The gate beneath Bleak Beach What's in Bubbly Basin? Bubbly Basin is the first of three content waves included in the Pokémon Pokopia Expansion Pass. It introduces new Pokémon, new areas to build in, and new content tied to the underwater setting. For a full breakdown of every Pokémon confirmed for this wave, check out the complete Bubbly Basin Pokémon list . The DLC launched on August 5, 2026 alongside the v2.0.0 base game update, which also added free content for all players including the Dive ability , Universal Storage , and other changes. Owning the base game gets you those free additions regardless of whether you buy the pass. title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Unlock Dive Ability
description: Unlock the Dive ability in Pokémon Pokopia with our step-by-step guide. Complete Bleak Beach prerequisites, find Manaphy, and explore underwater.

The full list of requirements before you can even start the Dive questline: Complete Withered Wasteland Learn the Jump ability from Magikarp Unlock Bleak Beach Learn the Surf ability from Lapras Complete the 'Raise the Environment Level' request in Bleak Beach All five of these must be done before the Dive chain becomes available. Focus on building up that area's environment score before expecting Professor Tangrowth to send you anywhere new. Talk to Tangrowth first How to unlock Dive Once all five prerequisites are cleared, head to Bleak Beach and speak to Professor Tangrowth . He'll point you toward a new island in the area. The ability gets significantly more mileage if you have the Expansion Pass . Wave 1, which released August 5, 2026, introduces Bubbly Basin , a brand-new underwater environment with new Pokémon and content built entirely around the Dive mechanic. For base-game players, Dive still adds meaningful depth (literally) to Bleak Beach, just without the dedicated new zone. tip If you own the Expansion Pass, completing the Manaphy quest triggers a follow-up task that leads directly into Bubbly Basin. Base-game players still benefit from Dive in Bleak Beach, but the DLC chain won't activate. Build underwater habitats in Bleak Beach What comes next after unlocking Dive? With Dive in hand, Bleak Beach has a lot more to offer. Underwater building opens up new habitat options, and if you're working through the game's Pokémon collection, some species and resources are only accessible beneath the surface. title: Pokémon Pokopia Magnemite Skill Guide: How to Unlock Magnet Rise
description: Learn how to unlock Magnet Rise in Pokémon Pokopia, including how to help Magnemite, build the Factory Storage habitat, and use this powerful post-game building ability.
content: Ditto gains several skills and transformations throughout Pokémon Pokopia , but players might notice one empty slot still sitting on the skill wheel even after unlocking most abilities. That missing ability is Magnet Rise , the final transformation in the game. Magnet Rise is unlocked in the post-game , and it also turns out to be one of the most useful abilities for building and exploration. This guide explains how to unlock Magnet Rise, how to help Magnemite , and what the ability actually does. How to Unlock Magnet Rise Magnet Rise only becomes available after finishing the main story of Pokémon Pokopia. Once the credits roll and the player loads back into the world, Ditto will return to the same location where the mysterious tower used to stand earlier in the game. After the ending events, the tower is gone and a large hole remains in its place . Pokémon Pokopia Magnemite Skill Guide: How to Unlock Magnet Rise Players may have explored this underground area earlier by entering from the ocean side of the metal structure, but after completing the story something new appears. A Magnemite can now be found there. Talking to Magnemite starts a small quest. It asks the player to build a habitat so it can stay in the area. Completing this request unlocks the final transformation. ’s Habitat To help Magnemite , players must build the Factory Storage habitat . Most of the materials needed for this habitat can be found nearby, which makes the quest fairly quick to complete. The required items are: Jumbled Cords ×1 Streetlight (any type) ×1 Metal Drum ×1 Control Unit ×1 Pokémon Pokopia Magnemite Skill Guide: How to Unlock Magnet Rise The Metal Drum and Jumbled Cords are located close to where the quest begins, so players can collect them immediately. For the Streetlight , any variant works. Many players craft a Mushroom Lamp since it is easy to make and does not require electricity. The last item, the Control Unit , requires a short trip. Players must travel to Sparkling Skylands , specifically the northeast island filled with ruined offices and buildings . A Control Unit can be taken from one of the structures there. After collecting all the parts, return to the Withered Wasteland and place the Factory Storage habitat. Once the habitat is built, speak to Magnemite again to finish the quest. Magnemite then teaches Ditto the Magnet Rise transformation . What Magnet Rise Does Magnet Rise transforms Ditto into Magnemite , giving the player a completely different way to build and interact with the world. While using Magnet Rise, players can freely hover and move in all directions , which makes construction much easier. Instead of jumping around as regular Ditto , players can float around the area while placing blocks and furniture. Pokémon Pokopia Magnemite Skill Guide: How to Unlock Magnet Rise This transformation also acts like an advanced build mode . Players can quickly place structures, reposition objects, and collect materials much faster than normal. Magnet Rise even allows Ditto to absorb certain blocks and materials that could not be picked up before. Because of these advantages, Magnet Rise is widely considered one of the most useful abilities in Pokémon Pokopia, especially for players who enjoy decorating their island or building large structures. Why Magnet Rise Is Worth Unlocking Magnet Rise is the final skill for Ditto and essentially serves as the game’s ultimate building tool . The ability to fly around construction areas, gather blocks efficiently, and place structures quickly makes a huge difference when designing habitats or improving the island. This is also why many players recommend saving large building projects until after finishing the story , since Magnet Rise makes the process significantly easier. Once unlocked, it becomes the best way to shape Pokopia exactly the way players want.

title: Pokemon Pokopia Guide: Hpw to Use Security Cameras
description: Learn how to place, configure, and monitor security cameras in Pokemon Pokopia to track habitats and find rare Pokemon faster.
content: Security cameras in Pokemon Pokopia are one of the most practical tools at your disposal, letting you monitor habitats, track Pokemon spawns, and manage your island without running back and forth across the map. If you've been ignoring them, you're making your life a lot harder than it needs to be. How Do You Get Security Cameras in Pokopia? Before placing a single camera, you need to actually own one. Head to the shop, spend your Life Coins, and you're ready to start building your surveillance network. Buy security cameras here info Purchase multiple security cameras at once so you can monitor several habitats simultaneously without interrupting your workflow. How to Place and Configure Security Cameras in Pokopia Placement is everything with security cameras. You need to position each camera close to the specific spot you want to monitor, whether that's a habitat, a crop area, or a spawn zone you're watching for a particular Pokemon. Once you've placed a camera, inspect it immediately to check its current view. From the security camera menu , you have three controls available: Angle adjustment to shift the camera's field of view Zoom in to focus on a specific point within the frame Zoom out to capture a wider area Take a moment to fine-tune each camera after placing it. A poorly angled camera that misses the spawn point you're targeting defeats the purpose entirely. danger Position cameras as close as possible to your target area. While the wireless range is generous, closer placement gives you a cleaner, more useful view of the exact spot you're monitoring. Adjust camera angle and zoom How to View Your Security Camera Live Feed Placing cameras is only half the job. Knowing how to access their feeds quickly is what makes the system genuinely useful. Here's the exact process to check your cameras: Open your Pokedex menu Select the Camera app Navigate to the Security Cameras tab Cycle through each camera's live feed if you have multiple placed The ability to cycle through multiple feeds from a single menu means you can survey your entire island in seconds rather than physically traveling to each location. info If you've placed several cameras across different habitats, cycling through feeds in the Security Cameras tab is far faster than fast traveling between locations to check on spawns manually. What Are the Best Uses for Security Cameras in Pokopia? Security cameras shine in a few specific situations. Here's where they add the most value: Use Case Why Cameras Help Tracking rare Pokemon spawns Get notified when a target Pokemon appears in a habitat Monitoring crop and habitat progress Check growth without physically visiting each area Finding undiscovered Pokemon Spot new arrivals passively while doing other tasks Managing large or spread-out islands Reduce travel time across the map significantly Watching specific habitat conditions Confirm environmental requirements are being met The notification system is particularly valuable when you're hunting a specific Pokemon. Rather than repeatedly running to a habitat and finding it empty, cameras alert you when something spawns there, so you can respond at the right moment. Taking Photos Directly From Camera Feeds Beyond monitoring, the security camera menu also lets you take pictures from the camera's perspective. Building a solid camera network pairs naturally with other island management strategies in Pokopia . title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Win Hide-and-Sneak
description: Learn how to win Hide-and-Sneak in Pokémon Pokopia. Use Camouflage, spot hunters fast, and reach the PC before time runs out.
content: Hide-and-Sneak is one of the most tense minigames in Pokémon Pokopia , and it can feel punishing until you understand exactly what you're up against. You have 3 minutes to reach the PC inside the nearby Pokémon Center without getting caught by a group of hunters. Sounds simple. Isn't. Here's everything you need to know to stop losing and start winning consistently. How does Hide-and-Sneak work? The objective is straightforward: touch the PC at the Pokémon Center before the 3-minute timer expires. The obstacle is a group of hunter Pokémon patrolling the area around that same building. Get spotted and caught by any of them, and the round ends. The hunters' positions, patrol directions, and your own starting point shift each round, which means no two attempts play out identically. Zorua is always one of the hunters. The rest are drawn from a random pool each round, so you can't memorize a fixed set of threats from game to game. Spot hunters by their speech bubbles What's the fastest way to reach the PC undetected? The back route is your best friend. Hunters tend to cluster near the front entrance of the Pokémon Center, which makes a direct approach the riskiest path. Circling around to the rear of the building cuts through far less patrolled space and puts you at the PC with much less exposure. Before you move at all, use the Camouflage ability on yourself. Moving through the area in your regular form makes you significantly easier for hunters to spot. Camouflaging immediately after the round begins is one of the highest-impact actions you can take, so don't skip it in the rush to move. tip Camouflage first, move second. Skipping this step is the single most common reason players get caught early. Back route cuts hunter exposure How do you identify which Pokémon are hunters? Hunter Pokémon have speech bubbles floating above their heads. Any Pokémon without a speech bubble is safe to walk past freely. Scan the area in the first few seconds of each round and lock in who's hunting before you commit to a route. Moving without knowing where the hunters are is the fastest way to walk straight into one. Once you've identified the hunters, track their patrol directions as you move. They don't stand still, so a clear path can close off quickly if you're not watching. warning Don't assume last round's hunter positions carry over. The random selection resets every game, so always re-identify hunters from scratch. What should you do when a hunter spots you? When a hunter notices you, a question mark appears above their head and a heartbeat sound plays. The moment either of those signals hits, stop moving completely. Don't take another step. Stay frozen until the hunter turns away and resumes their patrol. Moving even slightly while that question mark is active will confirm their suspicion and end the round. This freeze mechanic is the most reliable escape tool in the game, and it works consistently as long as you react fast enough. Freeze the moment you see this Does placing furniture actually help? Yes, and it's underused. Any furniture or items you place in the playing area before a round starts can serve as cover to hide behind while navigating toward the PC. More objects in the environment means more options to break line of sight with hunters and more surfaces to use as Camouflage anchor points. If you're hitting a wall on a particularly rough run of attempts, stepping back and placing additional items around the field is a legitimate strategy reset. Check out the hidden furniture guide for a full breakdown of every item that can work in your favor here. tip Furniture placement is permanent between rounds, so you only need to set it up once. Arrange it before your first attempt and every subsequent run benefits automatically. Why does luck matter so much? Your starting position and the initial patrol directions of every hunter are randomized at the start of each round. Some configurations are genuinely harder than others, and there's no way to force a favorable layout. The good news is that applying the strategies above makes even difficult configurations manageable, and easier layouts will occasionally just hand you a clean run. The Camouflage approach, back-route preference, and freeze response cover the skill side of the equation. The rest is variance, and variance evens out over enough attempts. What comes after winning Hide-and-Sneak? Once you've secured a win, there's plenty more to dig into. The event tied to this minigame runs until July 27, so time is short if you're chasing the trophy and event rewards. For everything else Pokopia has to offer, the full Pokémon Pokopia strategy guides collection covers every major mechanic and challenge in the game.

title: Dandelion Lunchtime: Jumpluff Habitat & Recruitment Guide

content: Jumpluff , the final evolution of the Hoppip line, is a rare sight in Pokémon Pokopia.
