title: How to Get Lumber Fast in Pokopia (Complete Guide)
description: A complete guide on farming lumber efficiently, learning the Cut move from Scyther, and using the Chop specialty in Pokémon Pokopia.
content: How to Get Lumber Fast in Pokopia Lumber is one of the most essential resources in the early game of Pokémon Pokopia . You'll need it for everything from building your first habitats to restoring the Withered Wasteland Pokémon Center. While you might occasionally find small wood piles in the overworld, the most efficient way to get Lumber is through the Chop Specialty and the Cut Move . Key Steps to Get Lumber Find Scyther : Build a "Tree-Shaded Tall Grass" habitat. Learn Cut : Complete Scyther's request to learn the move. Collect Small Logs : Use Cut on trees or lumber piles. Process into Lumber : Give Small Logs to a Pokémon with the Chop Specialty . 1. How to Find Scyther Scyther is the first Pokémon you'll encounter that can help you with lumber. To attract one, you need to create its favorite habitat in the Withered Wasteland . Building the Tree-Shaded Tall Grass Habitat Requirements : Place 4 Tall Grass tiles around a Large Tree . Pro-Tips : Use Water Gun to water trees. Use Leafage (Press ZR to switch moves) to create the grass tiles. Wait for the grass to shake, indicating a Pokémon has arrived. 2. Learning the Cut Move Once Scyther appears, talk to it. It will have an orange speech bubble. Request : Scyther wants 2 Sturdy Sticks . Reward : It will teach you the Cut Move . Usage : Press ZR to cycle through your moves until you select Cut. 3. How to Get Small Logs Lumber cannot be gathered directly; you must first gather Small Logs . Where to find : Look for large piles of wood blocking paths around the Pokémon Center ruins. Action : Use your newly learned Cut move on these piles to break them into Small Logs. Warning : You can also cut down trees, but we recommend keeping them for Berries and habitats early on. 4. Processing Small Logs into Lumber This is where the Chop Specialty comes in. Scyther (and later Pokémon like Pinsir) has this ability. The Exchange : 1 Small Log = 5 Lumber . The Process : Give a Small Log to Scyther. It will begin "wailing away" at the log with its blades. Real-Time Crafting : It takes time to process. Since Pokopia uses a real-time clock, you can leave the game or explore, and the Pokémon will finish the job while you're away. Fast Farming Tip : Log in during the morning to hand over your logs, and they'll be ready for your building session in the evening! Lumber Requirements for Main Quests To rebuild the Withered Wasteland Pokémon Center , you will need 10 Lumber . This means you only need to process 2 Small Logs with Scyther's help. Summary Checklist Resource Source Method Small Logs Wood Piles / Trees Use Cut move Lumber Pokémon with Chop Specialty Process Small Logs Sturdy Sticks Ground Spawns Pick up manually Mastering this loop early is the key to mastering Pokopia's building mechanics!

title: Mosslax Guide: Location, Wake Up Quest & Boosts List
description: Everything you need to know about Mosslax in Pokémon Pokopia. Find its location in Bleak Beach, complete the 'Brighten Things Up!' quest, and master its 'Eat' specialty boosts.
content: In Pokémon Pokopia , Mosslax is a unique version of Snorlax that has slept for so long that moss has covered its body. Finding and waking Mosslax is a multi-step journey through Bleak Beach , but the rewards are well worth it. Once awake, Mosslax's Eat specialty provides powerful gameplay boosts that can help you find rare items, attract more Pokémon, or even get discounts at the shop. Where to Find Mosslax You can find Mosslax in Bleak Beach , an area accessible after completing the Withered Wasteland Pokémon Center (past the first encounter with Drilbur ). From the Withered Wasteland entrance, head south toward the abandoned S.S. Anne . Turn left toward the beach hut and the stagnant water wheel. On the cliffside, you'll see several blocks. Use Rock Smash to break through. Mosslax is inside the lair, but it will remain asleep until you complete its specific questline. How to Wake Up Mosslax: "Brighten Things Up!" Waking Mosslax requires restoring light to Bleak Beach through the "Brighten Things Up!" questline. Before starting, ensure you've fixed the Pokémon Center and built habitats for Meowth and Trubbish . Step 1: Follow Trubbish Eventually, Trubbish will hear strange noises. Lead it to Mosslax's location (you may need to build some bridges). Step 2: Harbor Streetlights for Meowth Speak to Meowth in town. It will ask you to craft and place several Harbor Streetlights throughout the town. Use a Pokémon with the Generate specialty (like Pawmi ) to power them. Step 3: Torchic's Resort Habitat Torchic will task you with creating a Resort meal prep habitat . Head to the beach directly in front of Mosslax's lair. You'll find a campfire and palm tree already there. Add: Log Chair Plate Leppa Berry Step 4: Peakychu and the Shell Lamp A new Pokémon, Peakychu ( Pikachu ), will arrive in town. After meeting it, Peakychu will suggest using a Shell Lamp to brighten Mosslax's cave. Recipe : 2x Seashell, 2x Sea glass fragments. Action : Craft the lamp, place it in the cave, and power it with an electric Pokémon. Step 5: Windmill and Utility Poles Peakychu will lead you to the Windmill on the beach. Place a Utility Pole within the Windmill's vicinity to transfer power. Place a Harbor Streetlight next to the Utility Pole. Step 6: The Flash Device Finally, Peakychu will lead you to a device. Clear any blocks in the way. Connect the device to a power source using Utility Poles . Once all five bulbs on the device light up, Peakychu will absorb the energy and perform Flash , illuminating the entire town. Final Step: The Lightning Strike After the town is brightened, return to Mosslax. A final lightning strike from a new Pokémon will hit the cliffside, waking Mosslax and opening up a new path. Mosslax's Specialty: Eat Once befriended, you can utilize Mosslax's specialty, Eat . By offering food at its habitat, the Gourmet's Altar , you receive a special boost that lasts until the end of the in-game day (05:00 local time). Gourmet's Altar Requirements Core : Offering Dish. Item Preferences : Mosslax likes "Strange" and "Soft" items. List of Mosslax Boosts The effect depends on the Dominant Flavor of the food offered. Fully cooked meals (see our Cooking Guide ) provide a significantly stronger boost than raw berries. Dominant Flavor Effect Generic Increased rate of growing closer to Pokémon (Friendship) Bitter Increased chance of finding rare items Dry Increased chance to encounter Pokémon with rare feathers (e.g., Kyogre ?, Lugia, Ho-Oh) Sour 10% Shop Discount + Increased chance of "Good" shop items Spicy Increased chance of Pokémon appearing in habitats Sweet Increased chance of finding Ancient Artefacts tip If you're hunting for Legendaries like Lugia or Ho-Oh, offer Mosslax a Dry flavored meal (like Mushroom Soup) to maximize your chances of seeing rare feathers!

title: Pokemon Pokopia Photo Ops Guide
description: Unlock every Highlight Reel photo op in Pokemon Pokopia with this complete guide covering all requirements, rewards, and setup tips.
content: Pokemon Pokopia's camera system is one of its most charming features, but the Highlight Reel takes things beyond casual snapshots. These are scripted, one-time moments between your Pokemon and specific items or each other, and the game rewards you with exclusive photo frames for capturing them. Miss the notification, and that particular shot won't come back. Knowing exactly what to set up, and where, makes all the difference. What are Photo Ops in Pokemon Pokopia? Photo Ops are curated interactions that trigger under specific conditions as you build out your Pokopia community. When one is about to happen, a notification appears in the top right corner of your screen reading "Get your camera! A great photo op is happening nearby!" Press the - button on your left Joy-Con to pull out the camera immediately. Once the camera is open, follow the on-screen arrows toward the interaction. A border will appear around the Pokemon at the center of the moment. Take the shot using the in-game camera (not your Switch's screenshot button), and if the framing is correct, the photo op title flashes on screen and the image gets filed into your Highlight Reel under the Collections menu ( + button, then the Collection treasure chest). warning Using your Switch's built-in screenshot feature instead of the in-game camera will NOT register the photo op. Always use the in-game camera. Each Photo Op only triggers once. After you capture it, that specific scripted moment won't repeat, though you can still photograph your Pokemon freely at any time. Photo op alert notification How do you increase your chances of triggering Photo Ops? You cannot force most Photo Ops to fire on demand, but you can stack the odds in your favor. The key is placing the relevant items throughout your habitats before the notification has any chance to appear. A campfire sitting in a Pokemon's habitat is far more likely to produce the "Toasty Warm by the Campfire " moment than one you haven't placed yet. info Place multiple copies of key items like campfires, perches, and hot springs across different habitats. More exposure means more chances for the notification to fire. All Photo Ops and their requirements The table below covers every confirmed Photo Op in the Highlight Reel, what you need to trigger it, and any rewards it unlocks. Photo Op Requirement Reward Toasty Warm by the Campfire Any Pokemon relaxing near a Campfire Fire Spin Photo Frame A Gust of Wind to Get It Spinning Any Flying-type Pokemon spinning a Pinwheel with its wings None confirmed Punching Past the Sound Barrier Hitmonchan using a Punching Bag Impact Photo Frame Spacious Slumber Party Multiple Pokemon napping together (bench or large bed helps) None confirmed Greetings from Beyond the Grave A Ghost-type Pokemon interacting with a Gravestone Mysterious Frame Fun in the Sand Any Pokemon playing in a Sandbox Dust Cloud Photo Frame Found Some Delicious... Trash? Trubbish nibbling on Trash None confirmed Nothing Like a Quick Dip! Any Pokemon using a Sprinkler or Shower Bubble Photo Frame Stacking Blocks, Psychic Style A Psychic-type Pokemon playing with Wooden Toy Blocks None confirmed Battin' Around the Old Yarn Meowth playing with Knitting Supplies None confirmed A Cool, Gentle Breeze Any Pokemon interacting with a Fan None confirmed Roost and Rest A Flying-type Pokemon napping on a Perch None confirmed This Is the Life Any Pokemon soaking in a Hot Spring None confirmed Sweet Dreams with a Mossy Pillow Any Pokemon napping on Moss or near a mossy rock None confirmed Open It Up, and— Boo! Any Pokemon playing with the Boo-in-the-Box Lost Relic (L) Keep Out Photo Frame Martial Arts Training Montage Two Fighting-type Pokemon ( Hitmonchan , Hitmonlee , or Hitmontop ) sparring None confirmed The Skyland Specialists Tinkmaster and Conkeldurr interacting None confirmed No, My Horns Are Better! Heracross and Pinsir arguing near Graveler None confirmed Step Right Up, Step Right Up! A Pokemon with the Trade specialty at a Register None confirmed A Hypnotizing Lullaby Jigglypuff singing on a stage None confirmed A Cook's Gotta Eat Too! Chef Dente enjoying a meal (triggers at Rocky Ridges party if missed) None confirmed A Head Full of Blooming Flowers Mosslax's flowers blooming (only after completing Bleak Beach) None confirmed DJ Droppin' the Beats! DJ Rotom playing music for another Pokemon None confirmed Photo Ops that need specific setup Some of these won't happen organically without deliberate preparation. Here are the ones worth planning around: Open It Up, and— Boo! This one requires the Boo-in-the-Box , a Lost Relic item classified as size (L). You need to find it first, then place it somewhere your Pokemon can reach and interact with it. The payoff is worth the effort: Vespiquen getting startled by a Gengar popping out is genuinely one of the funnier moments in the game, and it unlocks the Keep Out Photo Frame . Greetings from Beyond the Grave You need a Gravestone item placed in a habitat where Ghost-type Pokemon live. Gastly is confirmed to trigger this one. If you haven't built a Ghost-type habitat yet, this won't fire naturally. Highlight Reel collection album No, My Horns Are Better! This requires both Heracross and Pinsir to be living in your Pokopia simultaneously. Both need to be in a position where they can interact with each other, and the game uses Graveler as a prop in their argument. Make sure both are housed before expecting this notification. A Head Full of Blooming Flowers This is story-locked. You cannot access this Photo Op until after completing the Bleak Beach storyline . Once that's done, Mosslax's flowers will eventually bloom and trigger the notification. How to view your completed Highlight Reel All captured Photo Ops are stored in the Highlight Reel section of your Collections menu. Press + to open the main menu, select the Collection treasure chest, then navigate to the Highlight Reel tab. Every photo taken through a Photo Op notification will have a pink camera icon in the bottom-left corner to distinguish it from regular snapshots. Your in-game photo album does have a storage limit, but any photo can be exported directly to your Nintendo Switch's system gallery from within the album. This means you can clear space without losing your Highlight Reel shots permanently. Tips for completing the full Highlight Reel faster Build diverse habitats early. The more varied your Pokemon housing, the more interactions you'll see. Campfires, perches, hot springs, and sprinklers should go in early. Don't ignore Lost Relics. The Boo-in-the-Box is a Lost Relic (L), meaning it's found out in the world rather than crafted. Keep an eye out for it during exploration. House rival Pokemon together. Heracross and Pinsir , Hitmonchan and Hitmonlee , Tinkmaster and Conkeldurr : these pairs need to coexist in your community to trigger their respective moments. Complete story beats. Bleak Beach and Rocky Ridges both gate specific Photo Ops. Progressing the main story unlocks them. Check your Highlight Reel regularly. Seeing what's already captured helps you identify gaps and figure out which items or Pokemon you're still missing. For a deeper look at building the right habitats to support these interactions, the Photo Ops guide on IGN) covers confirmed examples for several of the trickier shots. You can also find more Pokemon Pokopia tips and other gaming guides at GAMESgg .

title: Pokopia Shiny Hunting Guide (2026): Are There Shinies or Unique Variants?
description: No, traditional shiny Pokemon do not spawn in Pokopia right now. Learn how unique variants work, where event-exclusive Pokemon come from, and what to farm instead of shiny odds.
content: Pokémon Pokopia Shiny Guide TL;DR Pokopia currently does not use the classic random shiny system seen in mainline games. Instead, the game focuses on unique one-per-species identities and special event or story variants. If you are hunting "rare-looking" Pokemon, your best path is to follow event updates, complete request chains, and improve your habitat progression instead of resetting for odds. Treat this page as your decision shortcut: if your goal is collection value, prioritize event schedules, request rewards, and comfort/habitat milestones before spending time on traditional shiny methods. For many veteran Trainers, Shiny Hunting is the ultimate endgame. However, Pokémon Pokopia handles things a bit differently than traditional entries like Pokémon Scarlet & Violet or Pokémon Legends: Arceus . If you're looking for those elusive sparkling variants, here is the current state of Shiny Pokémon in Pokopia. Can You Find Shiny Pokémon in Pokopia? As of the current version, traditional Shiny Pokémon (random color variants with sparkles) do not appear in the wild. Why the Change? Unlike mainline games where you can catch hundreds of the same species, Pokopia is built on the concept of Unique Identities . There is only one Bulbasaur, one Scyther, and one Pikachu in your game world. Since each Pokémon is a unique individual with its own role in your ranch, the game does not support the "random spawn" mechanic required for traditional shiny hunting. Special "Unique" Pokémon While you won't find a "Shiny" in the traditional sense, Pokopia features Unique NPC Pokémon that stand out from their species with special designs, accessories, or alternate color palettes. Professor Tangrowth A perfect example is Professor Tangrowth . Appearance : Features a white "hair" top that makes it look like a distinguished scholar. Status : While it looks like a rare variant, it is a unique story-driven NPC rather than a random shiny spawn. Event-Exclusive Pokémon Keep an eye out for seasonal events! Most "Special" versions of Pokémon in Pokopia are tied to: Story Requests : Completing Important Requests for certain NPCs. Environment Milestones : Reaching high Environment or Comfort levels. Limited-Time Events : Such as the upcoming Hoppip event. Bubbly Basin DLC & New Pokémon The Bubbly Basin DLC (released August 5, 2026) introduces 50 new Water-type Pokémon to Pokopia. These Pokémon follow the same one-per-species rule as the base game. See the Bubbly Basin DLC Guide for details. There's also an upcoming Fetching Scales for Feebas event (August 13–28, 2026) bringing Feebas and Milotic to the Bubbly Basin. Will Shiny Hunting Be Added? The gaming community (including TheGamer and VGC ) is keeping a close watch. While the one-per-species rule makes random hunting difficult, there are theories about future updates: Costumes/Skins : Using items to change the "color" of your existing Pokémon. Dream Islands / Bubbly Basin : The Bubbly Basin DLC area introduces underwater exploration where non-unique Pokémon behavior may differ. Related Guides Pokopia Habitats Guide Pokopia Best Builds Guide Pokopia Game Length Guide FAQ Does Pokopia have real shiny odds like 1/4096? No. As of now, Pokopia does not run the standard random shiny odds system used in mainline Pokemon titles. Why do some Pokemon look different in screenshots? Those are usually special NPC or event variants, not random shiny spawns from repeated encounters. What should I farm instead of shiny encounters? Prioritize request progression, habitat upgrades, and event participation to unlock rare companions and unique visuals. Summary for Collectors Feature Traditional Games Pokémon Pokopia Shiny Odds 1/4096 (Base) N/A Hunting Method Masuda Method / Outbreaks N/A Special Variants Shiny Palettes Unique NPC Designs & Accessories Recruitment Catching Habitat Building & Requests Final Verdict : If you see a Pokémon that looks "different" in Pokopia, it's likely a Special Unique NPC or an Event Reward ! Cherish your unique partners, as there is literally no one else like them in your world.

title: How to Get Smooth Rock and Create Onix Habitat in Pokopia
description: A detailed guide on finding the elusive Smooth Rock and building the Smooth Tall Grass Habitat for Onix in Pokémon Pokopia.
content: In Pokémon Pokopia , building the Smooth Tall Grass Habitat for Onix during the "Yawn Up A Storm" quest is one of the first major hurdles for trainers. Finding the Smooth Rock and understanding the unique mechanics of gathering Dry Tall Grass are key to completing the request. This guide provides the exact location of the Smooth Rock and the specific steps to restore Onix's favorite habitat. How to get Smooth Rock in Pokopia The Smooth Rock is located inside the same cave where you first encounter and rescue Onix in the Withered Wasteland area. Precise Location Head back to the cave in the northwest corner of the Withered Wasteland . As you navigate deep into the cave (near where Onix was trapped), look toward the left side of the path. You will spot a red Poké Ball item pickup sitting on a shelf-like rock formation. Interact with the Poké Ball to collect the Smooth Rock . Visual Guide: The item pickup spot inside Onix's cave (Credit: Radio Times). [!NOTE] You do not need to craft or purchase the Smooth Rock. It is a one-time world item pickup essential for this quest. How to make Dry Tall Grass The most confusing part of the habitat recipe is obtaining Dry Tall Grass . Unlike regular grass, this item cannot be bought or crafted; it must be harvested using a specific Pokémon skill. The Leafage Trick Find a patch of Tall Grass on dry ground (ground that has NOT been watered). Use the move Leafage directly on the dry grass patch. The grass will transform into Dry Tall Grass , which you can then collect. Building the Smooth Tall Grass Habitat Once you have 1x Smooth Rock and 4x Dry Tall Grass , you are ready to assemble the habitat. Installation Layout Place the 4x Dry Tall Grass in a 2x2 square grid on the ground. Place the Smooth Rock immediately next to the 2x2 square. Layout: The correct 2x2 arrangement for the Onix habitat (Credit: Radio Times). When the arrangement is correct, a notification will appear confirming that the Smooth Tall Grass Habitat has been restored. You can then speak to Onix to finish the quest!

title: Squishy Clay Guide: How to Get and Use Bricks
description: Master the essential materials in Pokémon Pokopia. Learn where to find Squishy Clay and how to craft Bricks with the help of Fire-type Pokemon.
content: Squishy Clay is a foundational material in Pokémon Pokopia, required for crafting Bricks and various decorative furniture. Whether you're repairing the Poké Center at Bleak Beach or building a Stone Fireplace for your house, you'll need a steady supply of this clay. Where to Find Squishy Clay There are three primary ways to obtain Squishy Clay in the world of Pokopia. 1. Breaking Clay Blocks The most direct way to gather Squishy Clay is by destroying Clay Blocks found in the environment. These blocks are slightly lighter and browner than standard rock faces. Withered Wasteland Cave : Head to the northern cave where you first encounter Onix. Many clay blocks are located inside. Bleak Beach : This area is rich with clay. Once you unlock Bleak Beach through Trainer Rank progression, you can find blocks scattered across the shoreline. [!IMPORTANT] You must use the move Rock Smash or Rollout to break these blocks. Ensure one of your active Pokémon has learned these skills. 2. Ground Pokémon Drops (Litter Specialty) Certain Ground-type Pokémon have the Litter specialty, allows them to drop Squishy Clay over time in their habitats. Recommended Pokémon : Wooper, Clodsire, and Trapinch. Tip : Check your Paldean Wooper's habitat regularly for passive clay accumulation. How to Craft Bricks Squishy Clay cannot be used for construction in its raw form. You must process it into Bricks . Process: Show your Squishy Clay to a Fire-type Pokémon with the Burn specialty. The "Burn" Specialty To make bricks, you need a Pokémon with the Burn specialty. Early-game examples include Charmander and Torchic . Steps to Craft : Hold the Squishy Clay in your inventory. Speak to a Pokémon with the Burn specialty (e.g., Torchic). Select the option "Make me some Bricks!" . You can convert up to 10 Clays into 20 Bricks at once. Crafting Recipes Bricks and Squishy Clay are used in numerous recipes: Bricks : Brick Walls, Brick Flooring, Stone Fireplaces, and Planters. Raw Clay : Small Vases, Kitchenware, and Bathroom furniture. Item Required Material Amount Brick Squishy Clay 1 (yields 2) Small Vase Squishy Clay 2 Brick Wall Brick 5 Stone Fireplace Brick 10

title: Pokémon Pokopia Stardust Guide: How to Find and Use It
description: Learn where to find Stardust in Pokémon Pokopia, how to craft Star Pieces, and the two powerful ways to use them.
content: Stardust works very differently in Pokémon Pokopia than it does in earlier entries in the series. Forget selling it for quick Poké Dollars, this blocky island adventure puts Stardust to much more interesting work. It feeds into a crafting chain that can expand your Pokédex and unlock some of the rarest materials in the game. Here's everything you need to know about finding it, crafting with it, and spending it wisely. Where to Find Stardust in Pokémon Pokopia Dream Islands Are Your Only Source Stardust has exactly one origin in Pokémon Pokopia : Dream Islands . Every Dream Island you visit contains a generous spread of Stardust scattered across its terrain, and the material appears consistently across all of them. When searching each island, pay close attention to coastal areas and sandy spots , as these are the most reliable spawn zones. That said, don't skip the caves and interior locations either, since Stardust can appear in less obvious corners of the island too. info Visit a Dream Island every single day. Stardust respawns with each new daily cycle, so consistent visits are the fastest way to build up a large stockpile without any extra effort. Because you need 99 Stardust to craft a single Star Piece, daily collection habits matter a lot. According to Nintendo Life's guide, picking up every piece of Stardust on a Dream Island means it takes roughly two visits to surpass the 99-unit threshold. How to Craft Star Pieces Unlocking the Recipe The moment you pick up your very first Stardust , the game automatically unlocks the Star Piece recipe for you. There's nothing extra to do — the recipe appears immediately in your crafting options. What You Need The recipe is straightforward but material-heavy: Item Required Quantity Where to Craft Stardust 99 Crafting Bench (Other tab) Once you've gathered at least 99 Stardust , head to any crafting bench and find the Star Piece recipe under the Other tab. Craft it there and you're done. danger The Star Piece recipe sits specifically in the Other tab of the workbench, not in the general materials section. If you're having trouble finding it, make sure you've scrolled to that tab. What to Do With Star Pieces Star Pieces have two distinct uses in Pokémon Pokopia , and both of them are genuinely valuable. Neither use is casual — each one feeds directly into either Pokédex completion or high-tier crafting. How to Use Star Pieces to Expand Your Pokédex When you visit a friend's island through Link Play (online multiplayer), you can interact with their Pokémon. If you give a Star Piece to a Pokémon that isn't currently in your Pokédex, that Pokémon will offer you a Souvenir in return. Bring that Souvenir back to your own island and use it, and it will cause that specific Pokémon to spawn in your town — making it permanently yours to add to your collection. Gifting Star Piece to friend's Pokémon This is one of the most efficient methods for filling out your Pokédex with Pokémon you haven't encountered naturally yet. info You can only receive a Souvenir this way if the Pokémon you're gifting the Star Piece to is one you don't already have registered in your Pokédex. Gifting to a Pokémon you already own won't produce a useful result. How to Use Star Pieces With the Rarify Specialty The second use for Star Pieces involves Pokémon with the Rarify Specialty . Porygon2 is a confirmed example of a Pokémon that carries this skill. When you hand a Star Piece to a Rarify Pokémon, it converts that single Star Piece into a Rare Pokémetal . Rare Pokémetal is a high-tier crafting material with serious applications, including the ability to craft bells used to summon specific Legendary Pokémon . Porygon2 converts Star Pieces Tips for Efficient Stardust Farming Log in daily and head straight to a Dream Island to collect all available Stardust before doing anything else. Sweep the entire island , including caves and non-sandy areas, to make sure you don't leave any Stardust behind. Stockpile before crafting, having a buffer beyond 99 units means you can craft multiple Star Pieces in one session when you're ready. Decide your priority between Pokédex completion and Rare Pokémetal production before spending Star Pieces, since each use consumes the item entirely.

title: Team Initiation Challenge Guide - All Beach Building Requests & Deliveries
description: Master the 8-stage Team Initiation Challenge in Pokémon Pokopia. Learn all material requirements, from Leppa Berries to the Game Boy System, and roll the credits.
content: The Team Initiation Challenge is the ultimate questline in Pokémon Pokopia . Triggered upon your first visit to the beach in Withered Wasteland , this 8-stage "Important Request" acts as the final progression gate before the credits roll. To begin, simply examine the mysterious Tower on the beach. Challenge 1: Leppa Berries The Tower's first request is simple. You need to provide a small stockpile of stamina-restoring berries. Requirement : Leppa Berry × 10 Location : Shake trees throughout Withered Wasteland . Reward : Bouldery Badge Challenge 2: The Farm Essentials Now the Tower demands a variety of crops. You will need to have unlocked access to Bleak Beach and Rocky Ridges to complete this. Requirements : Bean × 10 Tomato × 10 Wheat × 10 Locations : Beans : Native to Withered Wasteland (near the Drilbur area). Tomatoes : Native to Bleak Beach . Wheat : Native to Rocky Ridges . Reward : Cascade-like Badge Challenge 3: Industrial Basics This stage introduces materials that require Specialties to process. Requirements : Lumber × 20 Fluff × 5 Paper × 10 Needed Skills : Lumber : Give Small Logs to a Pokémon with Cut (e.g., Scyther ). Fluff : Dropped by Pokémon with the Litter Specialty (e.g., Mareep ). Paper : Process Wastepaper using the Recycle Specialty (e.g., Trubbish ). Reward : Thunderish Badge Challenge 4: Heavy Construction The demands scale up significantly here. You must reach Sparkling Skylands to fulfill these requests. Requirements : Brick × 40 Gold Ingot × 20 Concrete × 50 Tips : Bricks : Use the Burn Specialty on Squishy Clay . Gold : Mine Gold Ore in the volcano (use Hamburger Steak to boost Rock Smash) and smelt it. Concrete : Use a Concrete Mixer and the Crush Specialty (e.g., Conkeldurr ) on Limestone . Reward : Rainbowish Badge Challenge 5: Powering the Tower You must now generate and harness electricity to activate the Tower's systems. Requirements : Electricity × 50 (Generated) Crystal Fragment × 10 Tinkagear × 5 How to Power : Build a Waterwheel and a Furnace . Connect them to the red light on the left side of the Tower using Utility Poles or Wireless Power Transmitters. Reward : Soul-like Badge Challenge 6: The Furnishing Phase The mysterious inhabitants of the Tower seem to be moving in. You need to provide high-end furniture. Requirements : Industrial Bed × 4 Resort Light × 4 Office Desk × 4 How to Get : These recipes are unlocked by raising the Environment Level of various habitats. You can also find them as world drops (e.g., Desks in Sparkling Skylands). Reward : Marshy Badge Challenge 7: Modern Amenities This is the final "material" challenge. It requires the most advanced electrical appliances in the game. Requirements : Washing Machine × 1 (Bleak Beach Env Level 5 reward) Refrigerator × 1 (Rocky Ridges Env Level 5 reward) Game Boy System × 1 (Sparkling Skylands Env Level 5 reward) Reward : Volcanoey Badge Challenge 8: Memories and Celebration The final task is a sentimental one. Requirements : A Photo : Choose any photo from your gallery. Party Popper × 2 (Recipe: 1x Paper + 1x Vine Rope ) Reward : Earth Badge & The Final Cutscene Once you deliver the Party Poppers, the credits will roll. Congratulations on completing the Team Initiation Challenge !

title: Pokémon Pokopia: Team Initiation Challenge Complete Walkthrough
description: Master the central end-game quest of Pokémon Pokopia: the Team Initiation Challenge. Comprehensive guide for all 8 stages, building requests, and material locations.
content: Early in Pokémon Pokopia , you'll be enrolled in the Team Initiation Challenge . Located at the mysterious tower on the beach of the Withered Wasteland , this challenge is not just a series of fetch quests—it is the essential journey to trigger the game's finale and roll the credits. Challenge 1 - Leppa Berries The first challenge is simple: bring the tower 10x Leppa Berries . Location : You can shake trees around the Withered Wasteland. Reward : Bouldery Badge . Challenge 2 - Beans, Tomatoes, Wheat For the second stage, you need to deliver 10 of each crop. Beans : Found natively in Withered Wasteland, near the ruined buildings where you meet Drilbur. Tomatoes : The native crop of Bleak Beach . Found near the first bridge. Wheat : Found in Rocky Ridges . Head left from the Pokémon Center. Reward : Cascade-like Badge . Challenge 3 - Lumber, Fluff, Paper This stage relies on Pokémon Specialties : 20x Lumber : Give Small Logs to a Pokémon with the Cut specialty (e.g., Scyther). 5x Fluff : Dropped by Pokémon with the Litter specialty (e.g., Mareep). 10x Paper : Give Wastepaper to a Pokémon with the Recycle specialty (e.g., Trubbish). Reward : Thunderish Badge . Challenge 4 - Bricks, Gold Ingots, Concrete The demands increase significantly as you reach Sparkling Skylands : 40x Bricks : Use the Burn specialty (e.g., Charmander) on Squishy Clay . 20x Gold Ingots : Smelt Gold Ore in a furnace with a Burn specialty Pokémon. Gold Ore is found deep in Rocky Ridges or Volcanic Dream Islands. 50x Concrete : Use a Concrete Mixer and a Pokémon with the Crush specialty (e.g., Conkeldurr) on Limestone . Reward : Rainbowish Badge . Challenge 5 - Electricity, Crystal Fragments, Tinkagears Time to power up the tower! 50x Electricity : Build a Waterwheel or Windmill and connect it to the tower using Utility Poles . Ensure your Generators are fully fueled. 10x Crystal Fragments : Found inside Rocky Ridges mines. Use Rock Smash on blue crystals. 5x Tinkagears : Crafted by Tinkmaster in Sparkling Skylands using Iron Ingots . Reward : Soul-like Badge . Challenge 6 - Industrial Furniture You must deliver 4 of each specialized furniture item: 4x Industrial Beds : (2x Iron Ingot, 2x Fluff, 2x Lumber) 4x Resort Lights : (1x Iron Ore, 1x Vine Rope, 1x Sea Glass Fragment) 4x Office Desks : (2x Pokémetal) Pro Tip : If recipes aren't showing, raise the Environment Level of your regions to Level 4 or 5. Reward : Marshy Badge . Challenge 7 - Washing Machine, Refrigerator, Game Boy System The penultimate challenge requires high-end electronics unlocked by reaching Environment Level 5 : Washing Machine : Reach Level 5 in Bleak Beach . Refrigerator : Reach Level 5 in Rocky Ridges . Game Boy System : Reach Level 5 in Sparkling Skylands . Reward : Volcanoey Badge . Challenge 8 - A Photo & Party Poppers The final step is purely celebratory. Hand in your most-cherished photo from your album and provide some party supplies. 2x Party Poppers : (1x Paper, 1x Vine Rope). Reward : Earth Badge . The Ending: Rocket Launch Completing all 8 stages triggers the grand Rocket Launch cinematic. This marks your official "initiation" into the Pokopia team and brings the main story to its emotional conclusion. [!IMPORTANT] To truly beat the game, you may need to complete other side-quests as well. Check our Ending Guide for more details. Want more tips? Visit: Guide Center

title: Pokémon Pokopia Version 2.0.0 Patch Notes: Every Change Explained
description: Pokémon Pokopia's Version 2.0.0 is live. Get the full patch notes breakdown covering Dive, new items, QoL improvements, and every bug fix.
content: Pokémon Pokopia just received its largest update since launch, and Version 2.0.0 is a substantial one. Released on August 4, 2026, the patch arrives alongside the Bubbly Basin DLC (Part 1 of the Expansion Pass) and brings close to 100 individual changes spanning new features, quality-of-life improvements, and bug fixes. Pokopia has already sold 4 million copies and sits among the top-performing Switch 2 titles, so Nintendo clearly has long-term plans for the game. Here's every change worth knowing about. What's new in Version 2.0.0? The headline addition is Dive , a new move that lets you move freely underwater. To learn it, you need to already know Surf and complete the "Raise the environment level!" request at Bleak Beach . Once you have Dive, the Build specialty can be used to construct houses underwater, which ties directly into the new Bubbly Basin DLC content. Beyond Dive, the update adds a handful of genuinely useful items and cosmetics: Portal pod and safe (recipes purchasable after raising Palette Town's environment level) Dynamic Ditto print pattern (talk to Smearguru after earning the diploma ) Two new emotes: Lie Down and Ready, Set, Go! (found at Bleak Beach and Dream Islands) Five new hair colors: orange, light pink, yellow-green, blue-green, and brown tip The portal pod recipe won't appear in the shop until you've raised Palette Town's environment level, so prioritize that if you want access to the new storage options early. Dive unlocks full underwater play The paintable items list also expanded significantly. You can now paint the stylish stool , handrail , metal chain , workbench , vending machine , bike , bookcase , Pokémon Center counter , arrow sign , and rope . What quality-of-life improvements does 2.0.0 bring? This is where the update earns its size. The improvements list is long and touches almost every system in the game. Movement and exploration Pokémon companions can now follow you while using Surf, Glide, Rollout, or Magnet Rise, which was a noticeable gap in the base game. Rollout got several upgrades: you can inhale items and open your bag mid-roll, and it can now destroy large boulders. Surf can be activated on land by holding the focus button and pressing Surf, and both Surf and Waterfall trigger more smoothly. Strength now works underwater, and Leafage can revert farm soil back to a normal soil block. Rollout now clears large boulders Building and crafting The power generator placement cap doubled from 64 to 128 (furnaces excluded). Photo display slots in a town jumped from 10 to 40. Crafting now pulls materials from the storage box next to the workbench before touching your bag, which saves a lot of manual shuffling. The 3D Printer now gives clearer messaging when you're short on materials. Pokémon not assigned to the Build role during construction can now help with cooking, so your crew stays productive. Buildings with items like the Ditto Flag attached to roofs or walls now clearly show they can still be remodeled. Loading table... Pokémon behavior and interactions If you destroy a Pokémon's habitat and rebuild it in roughly the same area, they'll move back in. Pokémon that got upset over removed furniture now notice replacements faster. The emote response system got a nice touch: Pokémon that taught you an emote will now mirror it back when you use it around them. Conversation indicators were thinned out so special requests and Ditto -directed dialogue stand out more clearly. The Pokédex now has an All tab (same for the Habitat Dex), and if a Pokémon you're searching for is in another town, you can travel there directly via Return Home. tip Smearguru can now learn patterns from photos stored in your References, opening up more customization options without needing to track down patterns through other means. and liquid mechanics The liquid system got cleaner. Holding the move button briefly while sucking up liquid keeps it in Ditto 's mouth without removing it from the environment. Released water now auto-matches nearby water levels. Certain roof items block water , which matters for anyone building near water sources. Tidal Bell and Clear Bell can now be triggered by laser sensors and switches. tip If you've been manually adjusting water levels after placing or moving water sources, the auto-level feature in 2.0.0 removes that step entirely. Water levels now auto-adjust Interface and settings Two new settings options landed: one hides the Magnet Rise cancellation confirmation message, and another lets you move while the move wheel is open. Motion-sickness reduction settings were added for the camera. Bulk item transfer between your storage box and bag is now possible, and you can delete items from inside objects like the garbage bin . Depth placement for windows and doors got finer control. The hide-and-sneak action can now be canceled mid-sequence. For builders, items can now be placed on top of square plants, and the game makes it clearer when and why certain build or relocation actions aren't available. What bugs were fixed? The fixes list covers 25 confirmed issues. Several are worth calling out specifically: Suicune and Gholdengo were sometimes unable to cross water , which is now resolved Pokémon assigned to building construction occasionally blocked the "Follow me!" option from appearing Honey sometimes failed to bring Pokémon back to their habitats Magnet Rise was occasionally triggering Pokémon scolding behavior incorrectly Pokémon requests could ask for items the requesting Pokémon actually dislikes (that's a rough one) Painting bugs: items consuming more paint than intended, surface light colors not updating, and unpaintable areas being paintable through specific steps A duplicate party cooking pot exploit under specific conditions Dream Island loading failures and incorrect post-Dream-Island teleportation to Palette Town Cloud Island multiplayer issues including non-admins placing relocation kits and building becoming stuck Rock Smash while falling displacing Ditto 's position significantly Quest-specific bugs in Withered Wasteland ( Slowpoke stopping mid-request) and Sparkling Skylands (Tinkmaster tracking and progression issues) Gender pronoun display errors on the Cloud Island loading screen in some languages warning If you were using the duplicate cooking pot exploit in multiplayer, that's patched in 2.0.0. Any setups relying on it will need to be rebuilt. Pokédex All tab now live What comes with the Bubbly Basin DLC? Version 2.0.0 launched alongside Bubbly Basin , Part 1 of the Pokémon Pokopia Expansion Pass. The Expansion Pass costs $34.99 and includes Part 2 (later in 2026) and Part 3 (2027). The underwater building mechanics added in this free update are clearly designed to support Bubbly Basin's content, so even free players benefit from the Dive and underwater construction additions. For a full list of Pokémon included in the DLC, check out our Bubbly Basin Pokémon guide . If you're still getting your footing with core systems, the Pokémon Pokopia beginner's guide covers everything from early progression to island building fundamentals. For a deeper look at how the game holds up overall, read our Pokémon Pokopia review . And for all guides covering mechanics, items, and secrets, browse the full Pokémon Pokopia guide collection .

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: Where to Find Cotton Spores
description: Learn where to find Cotton Spores in Pokémon Pokopia, how to farm them on Dream Islands, and how to use them at Hoppip’s event shop during the More Spores for Hoppip event.
content: Cotton Spores are a limited-time event material in Pokémon Pokopia tied to the More Spores for Hoppip event running during March 2026. Players mainly use this resource to buy special decorative items from Hoppip ’s shop located in the Withered Wasteland Pokémon Center . These items are not just collectibles. Many of them are required to build themed Habitats that attract event Pokémon like Hoppip, Skiploom, and Jumpluff . Because of that, gathering Cotton Spores consistently during the event is important if players want to complete the full event collection. This guide explains where to find Cotton Spores , how to farm them efficiently, and what they are used for in Pokémon Pokopia. How to Get Cotton Spores Cotton Spores are found on Dream Islands , which players can visit using Dolls. Once inside a Dream Island, the material appears as floating clusters scattered across the map . To collect them, players only need to walk up to the cluster and press Y to pick them up, similar to other gathering materials in the game. Pokémon Pokopia Guide: Where to Find Cotton Spores The spores can spawn anywhere around the island, so exploration is key. A simple route that works well is starting around the outer edges of the island , then gradually moving toward the center. After that, checking both the lowest and highest areas of the island helps catch any clusters that might have spawned on slopes or elevated sections. Most Dream Island runs typically reward around 40 to 75 Cotton Spores per visit , depending on how thoroughly the island is searched. Because Dream Islands refresh regularly, players can repeat this process throughout the event to build up a large stockpile. How to Use Cotton Spores Cotton Spores are mainly used at Hoppip ’s event shop in the Withered Wasteland Pokémon Center during the More Spores for Hoppip event. The shop sells themed decorations that help players build specific Habitats designed to attract the event Pokémon line. Some items are purely decorative, while others are required pieces for Habitat setups tied to Hoppip , Skiploom , and Jumpluff encounters. Here are the items available in Hoppip ’s shop and their Cotton Spore costs: Item Name Cost ( Cotton Spores ) Needed For Dandy Flower Clusters 5 Yellow Carpet Habitat, Dandelion Lunchtime Habitat Juice Trio 5 N/A Flower Garland 5 N/A Lunch Box 5 Field-trip Friends Habitat, Dandelion Lunchtime Habitat Hoppip Water Bottle 5 Field-trip Friends Habitat Flower Backpack 5 Field-trip Friends Habitat Flower Table 10 N/A Flower Cushion 10 Dandelion Lunchtime Habitat Flowery Table Setting 10 Dandelion Lunchtime Habitat Picnic Blanket 15 N/A Because several Habitat recipes require multiple decorations, players will likely need a large number of Cotton Spores to unlock everything during the event. Quick Farming Tips Players who want to gather Cotton Spores faster should keep a few things in mind: Always explore the entire Dream Island , including cliffs and lower paths. Follow a consistent search route from the edge toward the center. Visit Dream Islands daily to take advantage of resource respawns. With regular Dream Island runs, it becomes easy to gather enough Cotton Spores to purchase every item in Hoppip ’s event shop before the event ends.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Zorua Hide-and-Sneak Contest Guide
description: Master Zorua's Hide-and-Sneak contest in Pokémon Pokopia. Full reward table, fastest completion tips, and multiplayer rules.
content: Zorua 's Hide-and-Sneak contest is one of the more skill-testing limited-time events in Pokémon Pokopia , and the reward table is generous enough that it's worth grinding your personal best all week. The event runs until 4:59 a.m. local time on Monday, July 27, so there's still time to earn everything from basic crafting materials up to 50 Rare Pokémetal if you're fast enough. How does 's Hide-and-Sneak contest work? The setup is straightforward: sneak from your starting position to the PC terminal on the left side of the Pokémon Center entrance without being spotted by three seeking Pokémon. Your best completion time across all attempts determines which rewards you unlock, and each reward tier is earned once. To access the contest, you first need to have completed Zorua 's request in Bleak Beach and unlocked the hide-and-sneak ability. Once that's done and the event is live, logging in during the event period triggers a pop-up announcing that "a Pokémon is the talk of the town." Head to your nearest rebuilt Pokémon Center and Zorua will be wandering nearby. Talk to Zorua once to hear the rules, then talk again and select "is a Hide-and-Sneak contest going on right now?" to launch the minigame. important The event requires Ver. 1.1.1 of the game. Open the Options menu from the HOME Menu and confirm your software version before trying to start. Your system also needs to be connected to the internet the first time you play. Zorua contest rules screen What's the fastest way to complete the contest? The seeking Pokémon don't spot you the instant they notice movement. There's a brief suspicion window before you're actually caught, and that gap is the key to fast times. Using the camouflage move is the most reliable approach for beginners. When a seeker suspects you, stand completely still and they'll lose interest. For players pushing for faster times, you can actually keep sprinting for a split second after a Pokémon raises suspicion, and if you're close enough to the PC, just commit to the dash. The consistently fastest method comes down to location. Choose a Pokémon Center with minimal clutter around the back of the building. Start the minigame, use the building itself as cover on the approach, camouflage next to the closest object to the PC, then sprint the final stretch. After testing this approach across multiple attempts, completion times under 10 seconds are achievable, with a best of around 6 seconds using this exact method. tip If your current town has a lot of decorations and furniture near the Pokémon Center, the seeking Pokémon have more positions to patrol from. A cleaner environment around the building means fewer obstacles between you and the PC. Long grass cover near the PC Pokémon Pokopia 's Hide-and-Sneak contest rewards Every reward tier requires a new personal best time. Once you've claimed a reward, hitting that same time bracket again won't give you a second copy. The table below covers every tier from the most casual completion time down to the ultra-fast brackets that pay out Rare Pokémetal. Loading table... The Hide-and-Sneak Trophy at 1 minute 30 seconds is the only collectible unique to this event. Rainbow Feathers and Silver Feathers are valuable for players building out their Pokédex, but those can appear through other means. If you're purely optimizing for materials, clearing every tier under 20 seconds nets 50 Rare Pokémetal total, which is a solid haul from a single event. warning Each reward is granted once per player. Replaying the contest after claiming a tier won't duplicate the reward, so focus on improving your time rather than repeating the same run. Record set celebration screen How does multiplayer work for the Hide-and-Sneak contest? The contest supports two multiplayer formats, and the rules differ between them. Playing in another player's world: Both the host and any guests can participate together. The fastest time among all players becomes that town's best record, but only the host receives prizes. Spectator mode is not available. Playing on a Cloud Island: All players on the island can join the contest. The fastest time among all participants becomes the island's best record. Only the player who actually set that best time receives prizes. If you want to run the event from your own town in multiplayer using Link Play, use Palette Town. Before starting multiplayer, speak to Zorua first and receive the event details, otherwise the contest won't trigger for your session. tip The event also works on Cloud Islands outside of the standard multiplayer setup. If you're coordinating with friends to chase fast times together, a Cloud Island run lets everyone compete simultaneously. What else should you do before the event ends? If you haven't unlocked Zorua yet, that means Bleak Beach is still ahead of you. Keep progressing through the main requests until Zorua 's quest becomes available. The hide-and-sneak ability unlocked through that quest is the prerequisite for the entire event. For players who have already completed the Zorua quest and are working through the rest of Pokopia's content, the Zorua Hide & Seek event release date and start time guide has additional timing details worth checking before the July 27 deadline. This event pairs well with other ongoing collection goals. The hidden furniture guide is worth reading alongside this one if you're working toward photo ops and comfy boosts, since some of the materials earned here feed directly into habitat builds. The Bulbasaur Jump Rope Contest guide covers a similar timed minigame format if you want to compare strategies across both events. For everything else the game has to offer, the full Pokémon Pokopia strategy guides collection covers requests, habitat builds, item locations, and every other limited-time event.
